Content: Michael Carrick stayed in control during his press conference on Friday despite the first crisis of his managerial reign.Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick stayed in control during his press conference on Friday despite the first crisis of his managerial reign.Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesMichael Carrick‘It’s really not a drama’: Carrick sticks to the script after Martínez stormManchester United head coach produced a masterclass in dialling down emotion before a tricky trip to LeedsJamie JacksonFri 16 Oct 2026 15.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 15.16 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick returned his most impressive performance precisely when required as he took questions in the midst of the first crisis engulfing him as Manchester United’s manager.His team are bombing in the league after theclub’s poorest start since 1986andout of the Carabao Cup, and after Tuesday’s Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid Lisandro Martínez showed up ruptures at United bycalling out the director of football, Jason Wilcox.All of this two months into a first full campaign piloting United after last term ended so rosily for the former United midfielder.Carrick brushes off Martínez’s failure to apologise publicly to United director WilcoxRead moreOn the final day of last season,United won 3-0 at Brightonand Carrick secured an impressive third-place finish, 48 hours afteragreeing a two-year dealto continue as head coach.By last Saturday, United had six points from the first six games after drawing 1-1 with Tottenham at Old Trafford, placing Carrick’s job in jeopardy as the walls closed in on him a fortnight before the clocks go back.A game at Leeds in January proved to be Ruben Amorim’s last in charge at Manchester United after he greeted the 1-1 draw by demanding his colleaguesin the recruitment department “do their job”. With an uncanny circularity Carrick heads to Elland Road on Sunday after Martínez made similar comments. Amorim’s team were sixth going into that game; Carrick’s start the weekend 13th.On Friday, though, came a masterclass from Carrick in dialling down emotion as Martínez’s explosive comments about Wilcox – “I expect more [investment], 100%. I expect more from our technical director” – were addressed and he repeatedly referred to the “really good feeling” at the club.“It’s really not a drama for us as a group,” he said. “The boys have trained really well. This morning there was a really good feeling around the squad … so we’ve moved on pretty quickly.”If this seems less than credible, and almost certainly a stance coached by United’s PR mandarins, what else would Carrick be expected to say? More obvious was how the zen-like performance required from the club’s leader was being delivered. Even when he broke from the script to interrupt an inquisitor this strengthened the sense of Carrick being in control – hardly easy giventhe heightened glare on Unitedsince Tuesday evening.When the positive vibes trope was challenged by a questioner saying: “We’ll have to take you at face value”, Carrick’s interjection came with a smile. “I’m telling you the truth when I say that,” he said. “Do you not believe me, no? The players totally believe me. I’m telling you the truth. The squad today was in a fantastic place, better than I’ve seen it for a while, actually, and that’s it, plain and simple, you know? We’re emotional, we’re passionate, we care a lot.”When signing on to be the permanent United manager, Carrick had overseen only 21 games at elite level – in two caretaker spells at the club. United had 17 league games to play when he replaced Amorim, and Carrick has shown signs of faltering this season when having to compete on four fronts.Elimination by Brighton at the earliest stage of the Carabao Cup was not a great calling card regarding an ability to juggle competitions, and there was a surprising reaction from him after the2-0 opening-day loss at Hull. He bridled at the suggestion United had lacked “passion” during a first-half horror show. “Oh come,” Carrick said. “That’s ridiculous.”View image in fullscreenLisandro Martínez caused controversy for his post-match comments after Manchester United’s Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid.Photograph: Florencia Tan Jun/Uefa/Getty ImagesA faulty United rearguard is hampering an attack that is functioning far better and has the most shots (125) and most touches in the opposition box (205) in the Premier League. Nine goals from six matches is not paltry but greater ruthlessness would transform a promising front six into a potent one. Carrick has to find the right blend from Benjamin Sesko, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo, Marcus Rashford, Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBaleba has sparkled in his first two appearances – against Spurs and Atlético – and might have provided the shield from the No 6 berth to ensure a less leaky defence had he not arrived injured.This has to be the hope for Carrick. Playing Tielemans at No 10 at Atlético suggests the manager may doubt the 29-year-old’s legs, and questions have been raised about whether United are putting in enough of the hard yards. Their 671.4km distance covered in the league is the fifth-lowest (Arsenal’s 716.2km is the highest), and their 581 sprints the fourth-lowest (Brentford’s 765 the most).The trip to an always febrile Elland Road that saves a particular welcome for their cross-Pennines rivals presents a stern challenge. Leeds are ninth and have lost once.“It’s a great rivalry,” Carrick said, who was full of praise for his Leeds counterpart, Daniel Farke. “There’s big history between the clubs, the areas. That’s what makes these types of games special. You’ve got to embrace the history, what it means.“I’m sure it will be a fantastic atmosphere on Sunday. It brings an intensity and it’ll be a little bit extra again, on Sunday against us … Of course, we have to be ready, and the boys will be.”Carrick requires a positive result, though in denying this, he again sounded the right note. “I don’t need results, we all need results,” he said. “It’s not about me. Manchester United is a lot bigger than any individual, bigger than me, bigger than any player, anyone else who works at this club. It’s not about me, so please …“I don’t go into every day at work, in this situation, this game, thinking about me. It’s about what we stand for, what we live for, the history, the things that we need to live up to, and that’s what drives us. So whatever’s best for the club and for the team on Sunday is the most important thing.”Explore more on these topicsMichael CarrickManchester UnitedfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Gloucester upset odds to hold champions Bordeaux to draw in Champions Cup epic | Champions Cup | The Guardian
description: Gloucester and Bordeaux Bègles played out an enthralling 36-36 draw in the opening game of this season’s Champions Cup
Author: Robert Kitson
Headline: Gloucester and Bordeaux Bègles played out an enthralling 36-36 draw in the opening game of this season’s Champions Cup
Content: Will Trenholm roars with delight after Gloucester hold on for a draw with Bordeaux.Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenWill Trenholm roars with delight after Gloucester hold on for a draw with Bordeaux.Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/ReutersChampions CupGloucester upset odds to hold champions Bordeaux to draw in Champions Cup epicGloucester 36-36 Bordeaux BèglesWill Trenholm makes vital impact off bench for hostsRobert Kitsonat KingsholmFri 16 Oct 2026 17.05 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 18.20 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe new Champions Cup season is only just under way but thedefending champions Bordeauxare already having to battle for everything. The French side, chasing a third consecutive crown, were forced to weather a furious effort from a revitalised Gloucester in an outstanding contest and ultimately had to settle for a draw to complete a highly eventful visit to England.Four visiting players, including Louis Bielle-Biarrey, were held up for four hours on arrival by UK Border Control for failing to have a valid electronic travel authorisation (ETA), but stopping their star winger on the field tends to be slightly harder. The French international, in his familiar red scrum cap, darted over for two sharp tries but could not quite prevent the Cherry and Whites from claiming a share of the spoils.From star signings to Cullen’s last dance: six to watch in Champions Cup rugby this seasonRead moreGloucester had been given momentary hope by two tries within five minutes by their lively former Harlequins back-rower Will Trenholm, making a serious impact off the bench. The classy Bielle-Biarrey, though, dragged his side back level and either side could have nicked it in the final quarter. If this is a sign of what is to come in the tournament this season, it will be some ride between now and the final in Lyon in May.Bordeaux will certainly not forget this night in a hurry. In the absence of their injured French outside half Matthieu Jalibert, they picked their captain, Maxime Lucu, at No 10 but it was the deployment of their 150-kg prop Ben Tameifuna at lock that raised more eyebrows. In the event the Gloucester scrum mostly gave their opponents a hard time until Bordeaux cranked up the second-half pressure. “It’s bittersweet,” said Tameifuna. “We let ourselves down in the first half but our attitude in the second half was much better.”When they are in the mood the reigning champions have the ability to rip any opposition apart and they wasted little time in underlining their pedigree following a minute’s silence inhonour of Hyron Andrews, the Lions and former Sale player who tragically passed away in France before his side’s pool game against La Rochelle. The game was four minutes old when their scrum-half Martin Page-Relo nipped smartly down the blindside for the opening score with the versatile Lucu nonchalantly adding the conversion.This one-off round of pool matches, sandwiched into the busy early season domestic programme, still potentially offered an opportunity to catch them slightly off guard. Gloucester have made a promising start to their own Prem campaign and were full of early running on a cool, still evening.Arthur Clark crashed over to reward some sustained early pressure and there was plenty of interest, too, in Bordeaux’s first lineout throw. Would the massive Tameifuna suddenly soar like a mega-salmon? And would any of his teammates be brave enough to try and hoist him skywards? Unsurprisingly, when the moment came, the big man was used as a decoy having initially stationed himself at scrum-half.View image in fullscreenGloucester’s centre Seb Atkinson tackles the Bordeaux wing Louis Bielle-Biarrey.Photograph: Oli Scarff/AFP/Getty ImagesBig Ben was also soon to be found sucking in seagulls as Gloucester deliberately sought to raise the tempo. Again the ball was moved swiftly from the base and there was no denying the Welsh centre Max Llewellyn, one of six Wales-qualified players in the home 23, from close range. The lead did not last long, though, with another big visiting lump, Sipili Falatea, crashing over at the other end to make it 14-14.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe BreakdownThe latest rugby union news and analysis, plus all the week's action reviewedEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionA raking 55m penalty from the composed Lucu finally gave Bordeaux the lead for the first time but still Gloucester kept coming. The tweaked maul rule, making it illegal for opposing players to ‘swim around’ the side has been a popular decision in these parts and only some frantic defence from the visitors halted a concerted home drive.It was only a temporary reprieve. Once again the Gloucester scrum shunted forwards and George Barton rewarded his forwards’ hard work with another raucously-celebrated try. The Shed have been waiting for this fired-up, hungry version of ‘Glawster’ to turn up for years and, with Barton adding a further penalty, their 24-17 interval advantage was well merited.With over 60% possession and six clean breaks to one, the stats backed up that impression. There was never much doubt, though, that Bordeaux would raise their level and within 11 minutes of the restart they had two more tries on the board, the first scored by the winger Pablo Uberti courtesy of a lovely long pass from Bielle-Biarrey and the second from the prolific winger himself. Trenholm’s quickfire double, however, prompted another momentum shift and set up a finish as breathlessly compelling as everything that preceded it.Explore more on these topicsChampions CupGloucesterBordeaux BèglesRugby unionmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Wardley predicts ‘crazy night’ in fight for redemption against Dubois | Boxing | The Guardian
description: After losing his WBO heavyweight title in a brutal first bout in May, the Briton insists he can ‘right those wrongs’ in the rematch on Saturday night
Author: Donald McRae
Headline: After losing his WBO heavyweight title in a brutal first bout in May, the Briton insists he can ‘right those wrongs’ in the rematch on Saturday night
Content: Daniel Dubois (left) and Fabio Wardley will clash at the O2 Arena five months on from a Fight of the Year contender in Manchester.Photograph: Adam Davy/PAView image in fullscreenDaniel Dubois (left) and Fabio Wardley will clash at the O2 Arena five months on from a Fight of the Year contender in Manchester.Photograph: Adam Davy/PABoxingWardley predicts ‘crazy night’ in fight for redemption against DuboisAfter losing his WBO heavyweight title in a brutal first bout in May, the Briton insists he can ‘right those wrongs’ on Saturday nightDonald McRaeFri 16 Oct 2026 11.28 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 13.51 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFive months ago, watching alikely Fight of the Yearbetween Daniel Dubois and Fabio Wardley in Manchester, a ringside seat offered an initially thrilling insight into the raw brutality of heavyweight boxing. It was easy to be swept up in the drama as Wardley, defending his WBO title, dropped his more seasoned and favoured rival in the first and third rounds. But Dubois, whose courage had been questioned before, got up both times and fought back with admirable resolve.Dubois soontook control of the contestand administered a punishing beating, round after round, as concern for Wardley intensified. It was a worrying sight as the reeling champion refused to go down amid the damage being done to him by the bludgeoning power by Dubois. A terrible gash opened up across the bridge of Wardley’s nose and his face looked swollen. The end was finally confirmed in the 11th round, after the referee rescued Wardley from his own bravery, but it was the kind of heavy loss which takes years off a fighter’s career.Netflix’s Mike Tyson docuseries offers an incomplete portrait of a troubling figure | Andrew LawrenceRead moreWardley is one of the most intelligent and articulate fightersin Britain and it’s surprising that he has insisted on a rematch this Saturday night at the O2 Arena in London. A much longer rest, and then a far less perilous return to the ring, would have been a wise and pragmatic option. But the 31-year-old, whose previously unbeaten record was ruined by Dubois, insisted this week that “the thought of [their first fight] is worse than the reality. You put a bit of blood there, add some water and sweat and a punch that makes it spray everywhere, and all of a sudden it looks like a Quentin Tarantino film. It looks a bit mental.“But there was no real actual physical damage aside from cosmetically. There was a cut, but my nose wasn’t broken. I could still breathe fine, everything in good working order. I was just leaking a bit [of blood]. But I’ve been hit earlier in my career with harder shots that have rocked me more than anything that happened in the first fight between us.”He also suggested that fatigue, rather than the concussive force of Dubois’s punches, unravelled him. None of this really matches the sight of the weaving and broken figure Wardley resembled on that compelling but disturbing night in Manchester.At this week’s press conference Wardley added: “I was unlikely to get through this boxing game unscathed with an undefeated record, because I want to be in there with the best guys. And that puts you in jeopardy. I can right those wrongs. Now is the fun bit.”Dubois looked unimpressed and, in a typically terse response, dismissed any idea that Wardley would face anything but a night freighted with pain: “I’m feeling stronger, just grounded and ready to go out there and do my job. Do this thing and move on to bigger and better things.”View image in fullscreenDaniel Dubois recovered from two early knockdowns to stop Fabio Wardley in the 11th round in May.Photograph: Dave Thompson/APThe 29-year-old Dubois hasbeaten Anthony Joshuaand Filip Hrgovic, who nowholds the IBF versionof the world title, and he is a prohibitive favourite to beat Wardley again. “I’m a better fighter, an improved fighter,” Dubois said. “I’ll finish it quicker. I’m gonna school him again. That experience, and amateur background that you can’t buy, is what I’ve got on my side. Even without that, I’ve got his number. This time around, it’s going to be more clinical.”Wardley’s best chance might be to use his own considerable power early in another slugfest and hope that, this time, his punches overwhelm Dubois. “It’s only going one way,” Wardley said. “It’s finishing early one way or another. It’s going to be a crazy night. Everyone, tune in.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionDerek Chisora, the battered old warhorse of a heavyweight who is threatening to make yet another comeback to the ring, was scathing on the radio this week. “I think this is Wardley’s last fight,” Chisora said. “I believe he is concentrating on being a pundit. I don’t think he wants to box any more; I think this is a cash-out. Wardley is going to come out in the first three rounds and try to lay it on Daniel but, after three rounds, Daniel is going to get another knockout.”Wardley, instead, has insisted that he will use the experience of his two fights against Frazer Clarke to plot an unlikely victory. After he and Clarke fought each to a near standstill in a savage contest which ended as a blood-spattered draw in March 2024, also at the O2, Wardley dismantled the same man and knocked him out shockingly in just over two minutes seven months later. He believes that he can conjure up another startling turnaround against Dubois.But the cold hard logic of the ring suggests that, this time, Wardley is trading in dangerous fantasy.Explore more on these topicsBoxingfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: The Florian Wirtz mystery: why has he not found Leverkusen form at Liverpool? | Liverpool | The Guardian
description: Two of our writers pick over the German’s contribution to Liverpool and what the £116m forward could yet produce
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: Two of our writers pick over the German’s contribution to Liverpool and what the £116m forward could yet produce
Content: Shadow of himself: Florian Wirtz celebrates while playing for Bayer Leverkusen in 2024 and looks dejected after Liverpool conceded a second goal at Newcastle in 2026.Composite: Guardian Pictures; EPA-EFE/Shutterstock; Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenShadow of himself: Florian Wirtz celebrates while playing for Bayer Leverkusen in 2024 and looks dejected after Liverpool conceded a second goal at Newcastle in 2026.Composite: Guardian Pictures; EPA-EFE/Shutterstock; Getty ImagesLiverpoolThe Florian Wirtz mystery: why has he not found Leverkusen form at Liverpool?Two of our writers pick over the German’s contribution to Liverpool and what the £116m forward could yet produceAndy HunterandAndy BrassellFri 16 Oct 2026 12.40 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 12.42 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIs Wirtz struggling at Liverpool as badly as most outside observers believe?Some criticism has been OTT and a fee rising to £116m heightens demands but, yes, compared with his performances in Germany and for Germany Wirtz has underwhelmed at Liverpool. The past week has encapsulated his Liverpool career so far. In theChampions League rout of Laskhe was everywhere, exploiting gaps between and behind the Austrian club’s defence and knitting together a dominant display against limited opposition. In theprevious game against Manchester City, however, when Andoni Iraola needed big players to step up in the absence of Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai, Wirtz was ineffective, wasteful and withdrawn when his team were chasing the game at 0-1. It also did not help his cause that Rayan Cherki, a cheaper alternative whom Liverpool considered and passed on, completed City’s victory with a sublime goal.AHWhat are the main reasons for this?The physicality and intensity of the Premier League appear to be Wirtz’s biggest issues. He can be swamped, knocked aside, leaving Liverpool’s central midfield exposed. Iraola this week rejected the notion that the playmaker is struggling with English football, although his answer almost veered in support of the argument. “It’s not about whether they are foreign teams or English teams,” the head coach said. “It’s about different kinds of games. Some games are more comfortable, with more time to think, sometimes less. It’s not about the competition.” But, as Brentford are likely to demonstrate on Saturday, there is less time to think and little opportunity to get comfortable in the Premier League. Wirtz produced three assists in 11 Champions League games last season, the same amount as he did in 33 Premier League matches. His passing accuracy this season – from an admittedly small sample – is 80% in the Premier League and 91.5% in the Champions League.AHChart showing players with highest number of unsuccessful touches in the 2026-27 Premier LeagueDoes he have the ‘on-pitch personality’ to succeed at Liverpool?That is a question that can be levelled at many of Liverpool’s signings since the 2025 title win. The shift towards acquiring expensive “finished products” has left many pining for the hunger and spirit of emerging talent that characterised the club’s re-emergence under Jürgen Klopp. Wirtz does not have an ego to match his price tag. He is a conscientious, dedicated professional who Iraola, like Arne Slot before him, has found to be a good listener willing to put team instructions first. He is also, it seems easy to forget, only 23. Wirtz may not be a demonstrative force but he shows personality on the ball, always looking to receive it and take responsibility. His talent is clear but has not been seen consistently enough in a Liverpool shirt.AHWhat needs to happen tactically, and in general, for him to thrive at the club?Wirtz was sold on Slot’s vision for him as the central, creative force of a new-look Liverpool attack that would turn the slender wins of the title-winning season into dominant, emphatic victories. It never happened, and Slot was sacked without finding a position that best suited Wirtz. Iraola immediately confirmed Wirtz would be his No 10 and got to work on him building a close rapport with Isak. There were some promising signs before Isak got injured again. Wirtz can justifiably argue that forces beyond his control have conspired against him at Liverpool and that, as his relationship with Bradley Barcola and Isak improves, so will his end product. He would also be helped by the addition of an out-and-out defensive midfielder who could offer Wirtz licence to roam and greater protection to the Liverpool defence. Monaco’s Lamine Camara, whose proposed move to Chelsea collapsed on deadline day, is of interest.AHHow good was Wirtz at Bayer Leverkusen?Unbelievably so. In his final two seasons in theBundesligayou could make the case that he was the best player in it. He racked up goals and assists in European competition too (he was excellent in the Champions League in 2024-25 before injury halted him in the knockouts) but you can’t just describe it in terms of numbers. He dominated the big matches and acted as the conductor of Leverkusen’s orchestra. Teams who tried to kick him out of games almost universally failed, making the idea he can’t hack the Premier League physically a flawed explanation for his difficulties.ABChart showing leading players for combined goals and assists in the Bundesliga across 2023-24 and 2024-25How much of his success was down to ‘on-pitch personality’?Partly it was, but on a technical and tactical level his success was also partly down to the freedom Xabi Alonso allowed him. As Alonso said in November 2023 (during Leverkusen’sunbeaten double-winning season) every player had responsibility to patrol an allotted zone “but Flo is different” – he was given licence to prod opposing defences as he saw fit. Alonso’s rotation of him made sure he remained fresh and impactful, his hat-trick in the 5-0 win over Werder Bremen that clinched the title in 2024 coming after he was brought on as a half-time substitute.ABskip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIs the Bundesliga being weaker than the Premier League a factor?I don’t think we can say that isn’t a factor – but this is something Wirtz himself predicted. Many in his entourage thought he would be better served by joining Bayern Munich instead of Liverpool and he acknowledged he was taking the tougher option. He knew it was a risk but was determined to challenge himself. Another point is how different the Bundesliga is tactically; it has a similarly high tempo but is far more chaotic, which is perfect for a player with hissang froidto exploit.ABChart showing median Opta team strength rating of the clubs in Europe’s big five leaguesHe shone recently for Germany. Is he being used in a notably different way?He has been given greater freedom (and a little less responsibility off the ball), more akin to his Leverkusen role, but what has been important is having Klopp cheerlead for him. The manager has not missed an opportunity to say how great Wirtz is or how his good international form is “good for Liverpool”. Klopp also gave him the captaincy for the last game (and a half), showing Wirtz and the world that he believes not only in his talent and influence but in him as a leader. It feels like the more contact he has with Klopp, the better for him and his club.ABDo you have faith in Wirtz being a success at Liverpool?Wirtz can be a class act, a lovely footballer to watch, and it would be premature to write off a gifted talent who – as the previous answer about Isak and a defensive midfielder suggests – has not had the platform to fully express himself at Liverpool. But the question of whether the Premier League suits him and whether he suits this Liverpool team continues to gnaw away. Wirtz needed a strong start to the season after the difficulties of his debut campaign at Anfield and, with one assist and no goals in six Premier League appearances, that has not materialised. There was encouragement in his overall performance and in his understanding with Barcola against Lask, as there has been on several Champions League nights, but Iraola needs his playmaker to produce a repeat in games such as Brentford away. Wirtz will remain categorised as a luxury player if another difficult Premier League assignment passes him by.AHMaybe. The deck has been largely stacked against him since he arrived: there were too many changes to a champion team in the summer he arrived, plus he was expected to pull the strings in a side that still had Mohamed Salah. He has overcome big setbacks before, such as the 2022 anterior cruciate ligament injury that took a long while to get over, so he has the character to go with his class. Wirtz has the ability to succeed at Anfield but unless the conditions around him change I think it will be very hard to do so (I can imagine him being great for Bayern in a couple of years, post-Michael Olise).ABExplore more on these topicsLiverpoolBayer LeverkusenBundesligaEuropean club footballfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Premier League news: go bananas: Maresca loving fans’ show of defiance; Alonso backs his defence | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Manchester City manager embraces response to external criticism while Chelsea coach says ‘clean sheets will come’
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Manchester City manager embraces response to external criticism while Chelsea coach says ‘clean sheets will come’
Content: Manchester City fans celebrate at Liverpool.Photograph: Michael Regan/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenManchester City fans celebrate at Liverpool.Photograph: Michael Regan/Getty ImagesThe talkManchester CityPremier League news: go bananas: Maresca loving fans’ show of defiance; Alonso backs his defenceManchester City manager embraces response to external criticism while Chelsea coach says ‘clean sheets will come’Guardian sportFri 16 Oct 2026 17.30 EDTFirst published on Fri 16 Oct 2026 12.53 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google1.City manager says ‘we need to make our noise’Enzo Maresca has called on Manchester City fans to bring inflatable bananas to help inspire the team in their first Premier League home game since being foundguilty of financial breacheswhen they take on Ipswich on Saturday. Supporters packed the away end at Liverpool with the novelty items as a nod to the club’s history last weekend.Blow-up bananas becamepopular among City fans in the 1980s and 1990swhen they spent time in the second and third tiers, and have been revived in reaction to the threat of being punished with relegation and to show there is plenty to reflect on before the 2008 takeover.“Very nice,” Maresca said of the inflatables. “I didn’t know the history behind the banana. I hope tomorrow I can see many bananas in the stadium. I think it creates a nice environment for the fans and for everyone that is in the stadium. I have four kids, they already asked me [for bananas], but tomorrow they’re going to be at the stadium and we’ll see.”It comes after Maresca dropped points for the first time as City manager,losing 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germainin the Champions League. City are three points clear of second-placed Arsenal at the top of the Premier League and victory would make Maresca the first manager to win their first seven Premier League games with a club. City are playing against a backdrop of being the focus of anger around the country.“We need to try to make our noise,” Maresca said. “And to make our noise means win at Anfield, try to win tomorrow. And this is the way we can make our noise. The different kind of noise, we are not able to control that. I think Rúben [Dias] said that people don’t like the City win. But we like to win. So I think that is a good message for everyone. Probably since the noise, we can see, I can see from my personal point of view, the fans, the club, the team, more together for sure. But we’ll see.”Will Unwin2.Alonso insists ‘the clean sheets will come’Xabi Alonso has stressed the importance of clean sheets as he strives to find the right balance at Chelsea and faces up to the absence of Reece James for three months after knee surgery. The manager has been delighted with the attacking output of his team but it is a different story at the back where they have the joint-worst defensive record in the Premier League.Alonso made tactical tweaks for last Saturday’s 5-1 home win over Bournemouth when Moisés Caicedo returned in midfield to play alongside Jordan Henderson in James’s absence. Chelsea announced on Friday morning that James had undergone an operation; it compounds the captain’s reputation for bad luck where injuries are concerned.Alonso’s team defended deeper against Bournemouth and were compact in a 4-4-2 shape out of possession rather than their usual three centre-half system. There were positive signs, which Alonso is determined to build on at Everton on Saturday lunchtime.View image in fullscreenReece James has had surgery on a knee injury picked up in training before last weekend’s 5-1 win against Bournemouth.Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters“You need a lot of clean sheets to win trophies,” he said. “But you [also] need to score a lot of goals. So it’s about being strong in defence, being good in attack and we are in that process. We are still early days; to do a very deep analysis, it’s too early. We can maybe talk in February. Those tweaks … they need to come naturally and we are not in that moment yet.“The obsession is to win and to compete in the best possible way. The clean sheets will come, I’m pretty sure of that, because we want to play with good balance and good control.”The chemistry in midfield will be key and if Caicedo’s partnership with Henderson showed promise against Bournemouth, Alonso made it clear he would also count on Roméo Lavia and Valentín Barco. He added there would be matches where he played with three midfielders.“In terms of personalities, Moi and Hendo match very well,” Alonso said. “Hendo has this energy to go. He’s very active. He covers a lot of the pitch. And to find the balance with Moi … that he’s more in the position, that he has this stability to be in good distances with everything, it was a good start.“Roméo is in a good moment. He played very well with Belgium [during the recent international window]. He’s super available. It’s been difficult for him [with injuries] but this season he’s been available and has done really well. We need to keep him with the other midfielders because that area is fundamental for our game. And also Valentín. The minutes he has played with us, he has been very competitive. He doesn’t care who is the opponent. He goes. That warrior, fighting spirit he brings is very positive.”David Hytner3.Moyes backs Pickford to keep England shirtDavid Moyes believes Jordan Pickford will relish the challenge to his England place from James Trafford and remains the nation’s undisputed No 1 goalkeeper.Pickford and Trafford shared goalkeeping duties during the recent four-game international break as part of an arranged plan by manager Thomas Tuchel. The 24-year-old Leeds player is considered the biggest threat to emerge to Pickford’s long-held position with the national team but Moyes insists the Everton keeper has been sharper than ever this season.“When Jordan came back from the World Cup, it might be the best I have ever seen him,” the Everton manager said. “He was lean, he was sharp, his footwork was brilliant, he was fast across the goal and if you look at some of the saves he has made between now and then he has made a couple of brilliant, brilliant saves.“I spoke to him when he came back and said: ‘You know you have a bit of competition now with Trafford, how are you going to deal with it?’ I don’t see Jordan falling away at the moment. I think if it really mattered to England then Jordan would still be the one who was there because he makes saves. He did that in the Argentina game. He has that experience and he is not ageing.”Trafford has won plaudits for his footwork with Leeds and England. But Moyes reflected: “Jordan is a terrific kicker of the ball, he is a better kicker than Trafford, but passing is a different equation. When you talk about that, is goalkeeping now just about the passing? Or are you saying you still have to put your gloves on and make good saves and make good decisions. I think it would be hard to move Jordan off that role. I don’t think Jordan is moving aside at the moment.”Andy Hunter4.Iraola shares delight at coaching NgumohaAndoni Iraola has said it is “a privilege” to work with Rio Ngumoha and believes the Liverpool winger is on the path to becoming an elite talent. Ngumoha has shown his versatility this season, with the arrival of the £123m Bradley Barcola prompting Iraola to shift the 18-year-old to the right wing on occasion. Ngumoha helped create Barcola’s first goal for Liverpool when impressing from that position in the midweek Champions League rout of Lask.“For us it is a privilege to have Rio in the team because he has just become 18,” said the head coach. “He has already played some minutes with the national team and that is not normal. Normally you start playing with the national team when you are 20-something and you already have matured a little bit. We have to help him because luckily for us he is not the finished product. He can still improve because he is still 18 and I hope we can help him with these processes.”View image in fullscreenTrey Nyoni is likely to make his full Premier League debut for Liverpool at Brentford.Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPANgumoha won his third cap for England during the recent international break, featuring in both wins over Czechia in the Nations League, and has started four times for Liverpool under Iraola. “I think he knows he is elite at certain things,” Iraola said. “If you want to put someone one versus one then Rio is one of the best players you would choose because he is so difficult to contain.“There are areas he has to improve, especially without the ball. He has to get used to the demands of the Premier League in terms of duels and this happens when you come from the youth system. There you are used to being superior to the others and now you face very strong opposition and it is not easy to sustain those duels, but he is improving a lot. Body-wise he is becoming stronger and I think he is in a good place.”Andy Hunter5.Gibbs-White a doubt for Arsenal encounterNottingham Forest are sweating on the fitness of Morgan Gibbs-White before Sunday’s clash with Arsenal. The England international picked up a “minor” calf injury in last weekend’sdefeat at Crystal Palaceand will be assessed before the visit of the champions.“Morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt, he couldn’t train the entire week with us,” the manager, Oliver Glasner, said. “But it looks like he can join tomorrow’s session. He had an individual session today with our rehab coaches. Then we have to see how he reacts today and how he deals with tomorrow’s session, and then how we take the final decision.”Forest will also assess Nikola Milenkovic, who has returned to training after a bone bruise. “Milenkovic trained for the first time today,” Glasner said. “Let’s see now how he reacts. He could be in the matchday squad, but let’s see, because he’s now out for several weeks.”Press AssociationExplore more on these topicsManchester CityThe talkChelseaLiverpoolEvertonNottingham ForestnewsShareReuse this content

title: British Cycling under scrutiny over allegations of ‘toxic culture’ in leadership team | Cycling | The Guardian
description: A former commercial manager criticised the handling of a bullying complaint as British Cycling insisted ‘action is taken’ when appropriate
Author: Sean Ingle
Headline: A former commercial manager criticised the handling of a bullying complaint as British Cycling insisted ‘action is taken’ when appropriate
Content: A British Cycling survey found 31% of riders and staff said they had witnessed or experienced thoughtless, inappropriate, or unacceptable behaviour.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAView image in fullscreenA British Cycling survey found 31% of riders and staff said they had witnessed or experienced thoughtless, inappropriate, or unacceptable behaviour.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PACyclingBritish Cycling under scrutiny over allegations of ‘toxic culture’ in leadership teamFormer employee alleges bullying swept under carpetBritish Cycling defends handling of complaintsSean IngleFri 16 Oct 2026 13.07 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 15.28 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBritish Cycling is facing further questions after a former employee accused it of having a “toxic culture” days afterMatt Richardson was sent homefrom the World Track Championships in Shanghai.Jack Lindsay, who worked as a commercial manager atBritish Cyclingfrom 2024 to 2025, criticised the way he claimed it responded to his formal workplace bullying complaint spanning dozens of incidents. And he also questioned what he branded a lack of oversight from UK Sport, which has given the organisation £30m to prepare for the LA Olympics.“The complaint covered dozens of incidents over six months, spanning multiple categories of alleged bullying,” Lindsay wrote in a post on LinkedIn. “Most were partially substantiated. There would be no apology, and I was told of no action against the individual I had sought to hold responsible.”Matt Richardson vows to cooperate with investigation into alleged misconductRead moreLindsay also claimed that he had “repeatedly raised incidents of bullying by a member of the executive with members of the senior leadership team, and that management had chosen to address them informally”.“It is not acceptable to continue subjecting staff to a leadership team that have perpetuated this toxic culture,” he said.Lindsay said that after he resigned the-then BritishCyclingchief executive, Jon Dutton, told him that he would commission an independent survey of the leadership culture within the GB Cycling Team.That survey, it was revealed by the Times newspaper this week, found that 31% of riders and staff were asked whether they had “witnessed or experienced thoughtless, inappropriate, or unacceptable behaviour” answered yes.Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Meanwhile when they were asked for three words to describe the culture of their world class programme, “driven” was the most commonly used word among the riders but second-most prominent, alongside “supportive”, was “toxic”.In response to a series of questions about Lindsay’s allegations, a British Cycling spokesperson said: “The wellbeing of our people is fundamental to everything we do at British Cycling. Any complaint is taken seriously and handled through our formal procedures and where appropriate, action is taken.“Out of fairness to everyone involved, we do not comment on individual cases, and the details of any action taken are kept confidential,” he added. “We recognise that raising concerns can be difficult. There are established routes available to report concerns and we continue to strengthen how we listen to and support our people.”Lindsay also drew parallels with how British Cycling’s governance and culture had been heavily criticised by Annamarie Phelps in an independent review in 2017, saying that “almost a decade later, leadership is taking the program in the same direction”.“This reflects a wider problem in elite sport, where organisational reputation and relationships with funding bodies and the individuals within can become entangled with questions of accountability,” he wrote.“The high-performance programme receives millions of pounds each year in public funding. Athletes, staff, sponsors and the public have a legitimate interest in whether the organisation upholds the standards it promotes.”However a UK Sport spokesperson said that the organisation did properly hold sports accountable and that its approach was “fundamentally and materially different to 2017”.The spokesperson added that funded sports were required to “complete a cultural assurance exercise on an annual basis,” and to develop cultural action plans to strengthen and improve their culture. UK Sport said that a team of advisers was also in place to “provide assurance on our investment”.“It is critical to us that the sports we invest in have a safe, healthy and high performing culture where athlete voice is included in decision making,” the spokesperson added. “We prioritise assuring culture within the performance programmes in which we invest as a key pillar of our approach to winning well.”Explore more on these topicsCyclingBritish CyclingnewsShareReuse this content

title: England’s World Cup test against Tonga will show where power really lies in rugby league | Rugby League World Cup 2026 | The Guardian
description: England begin their tournament on Saturday with a must-win fixture in Perth that can inject some optimism into the European game
Author: Aaron Bower
Headline: England begin their tournament on Saturday with a must-win fixture in Perth that can inject some optimism into the European game
Content: Kai Pearce-Paul is part of an eye-catching England back row.Photograph: Anita Reca/SWpix.com/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenKai Pearce-Paul is part of an eye-catching England back row.Photograph: Anita Reca/SWpix.com/ShutterstockRugby League World Cup 2026England’s World Cup test against Tonga will show where power really lies in rugby leagueEngland begin their tournament on Saturday with a must-win fixture in Perth that can inject some optimism into the European gameAaron BowerFri 16 Oct 2026 10.22 EDTFirst published on Fri 16 Oct 2026 07.45 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTwo games into the men’s World Cup and the tournament is already overflowing with colour. As if the biggest Test crowd in Sydney for more than 50 years was not enough cause for celebration, Australia and New Zealand served up one of the great international games of modern times, with theKangaroos edging a thrilleron the opening night.But the stories do not end there. Samoa’s rise as a league powerhouse continued with a record win against France on Friday, with their passionate and united Pasifika fanbase fuelling the energy for a tilt at a second consecutive final. Tonga and Papua New Guinea will continue the theme of national pride and unforgettable noise this weekend.Nation-swappers show Rugby League World Cup is up for grabs in fiery opener | Angus FontaineRead moreThe decision several years ago from some of the NRL’s best players to honour their Pacific heritage and play for nations such as Samoa and Tonga rather than Australia and New Zealand has led us to a point where there is now a bigger pool of contenders to win the World Cup. An overarching lesson perhaps that bold decisions today can lead to brighter outcomes tomorrow.Spare a thought for the English game in all of this, though. England has felt like the long lost European cousin whose invite to the party has gone missing in the post. While all the fun is going on elsewhere, the supposed grownups are upstairs arguing yet again, after Super League missed the NRL’s deadline of Thursday to agree an historic partnership between the leagues.The discussion around why and what happens next is for another day but in England it has cast a shadow over what has felt a pretty low-key buildup. With the tournament tucked away behind a paywall on television, you would be forgiven for not even knowing there is a World Cup taking place at all despite a new-look national team entering the fray on Saturday with a chance to make a statement.Such is the truncated format this year, England are in must-win territory from the start when they face a tricky test against Tonga. Win, and passage through to the semi-finals should be safe given what is to follow. But slip up, and they may well be relying on results elsewhere – and a favour from Samoawho beat them in the semis in 2022– to progress.That makes their opening game in Perth intriguing enough. But so too does the narrative around England slipping beneath Samoa and Tonga in the pecking order. European rugby league already feels like a distant second; failure to reach the semi-finals for England this year would reinforce that thought.View image in fullscreenEngland head coach Brian McDermott keeps an eye on training in Perth.Photograph: Anita Reca/SWpix.com/ShutterstockIn a bid to counter that, Brian McDermott has promised England will try to do things differently. Last year’s Ashes felt like a missed opportunity – the Kangaroos were not tested or stretched enough. McDermott has been abundantly clear that to beat the best at international level, you cannot simply expect to meet fire with fire: you need to mix things up.“It’s definitely been different, I’m not going to tell you all the tricks of what we’ve got planned but it’s been different and enjoyable,” said England’s captain, George Williams. “The group have all bought into what he wants us to do and hopefully you’ll see that when we play against Tonga. I won’t give too much away but we’ll do some stuff you might not have seen before.”That is perhaps a discreet admission from Williams that England’s tactics in recent years have not met the grade. McDermott has kept his gameplan secret but there are clues in his team selection: more mobile, agile forwards who can promote second-phase rugby and bring an exciting backline into the game.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toSport in FocusOur picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown inEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWith the world’s best centre in Herbie Farnworth, try-scoring phenomena Dom Young and Zach Eckersley on the wings and an eye-catching back row pair of Junior Nsemba and Kai Pearce-Paul, England clearly have the talent to entertain. They will need to contend with a boisterous pro-Tongan crowd in Perth as well as a Mate Ma’a side which possesses physicality aplenty.Williams was brave enough to admit that “Tonga have got a stacked team so we’re underdogs, but we’ll embrace that tag”. McDermott normally keeps his cards close to his chest but he broke rank this week and insisted this group, together in Australia for just a week, have the potential to achieve something special. They must be faultless from minute one to do that.England may have dispatched Samoa and Tonga with relative ease on home soil since the last World Cup, but their shock defeat to the former in the semi-finals four years ago felt like a seismic moment for both the rise of Pasifika rugby league, and the fading of England into the shadows.Super League’s failure to agree an NRL deal has risked setting the European game back even further, but victory for England this weekend would provide some optimism. As has been the case so many times in recent years, it is over to the players to deliver that much-needed shot in the arm.Explore more on these topicsRugby League World Cup 2026Rugby League World CupEngland rugby league teamTongarugbyleagueteamRugby leaguefeaturesShareReuse this content

title: The WSL so far: goal-shy Arsenal, underrated Brighton and more data pointers | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: The Gunners’ title hopes look over after five games as draws continue from last season while the Seagulls, actually ninth, are third for expected points
Author: Andrew Beasley
Headline: The Gunners’ title hopes look over after five games as draws continue from last season while the Seagulls, actually ninth, are third for expected points
Content: Arsenal's Ona Batlle, Birmingham's Océane Hurtré, Brighton's Kiko Seike.Composite: Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenArsenal's Ona Batlle, Birmingham's Océane Hurtré, Brighton's Kiko Seike.Composite: Getty ImagesWomen's Super LeagueThe WSL so far: goal-shy Arsenal, underrated Brighton and more data pointersThe Gunners’ title hopes look over after five games as draws continue from last season while the Seagulls, actually ninth, are third for expected pointsAndrew BeasleyFri 16 Oct 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 11.14 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Women’s Super League table is taking shape for 2026-27. The defending champions, Manchester City, have five wins from five games but more intriguing stories lie elsewhere. Why are Arsenal struggling, who is performing better than results suggest, and in which way are two promoted teams smashing expectations? Here are three key data points.Arsenal have two major flawsOpta made Arsenal third favourites to win the WSL before a ball was kicked. Their win at Brighton combined with Chelsea’s draw against Aston Villa in week one meant Renée Slegers’ side rose to narrow favourites. The four games since, from which Arsenal took two points, have torpedoed their title chances.Chart showing the chance of winning the 2026-27 Women’s Super League by matchweek for Arsenal, Chelsea and Manchester CityOne reason for their slump is a continuation of a problem from last season. The stats section of our Arsenalpre-season previewhighlighted draws in 2025-26 that they deserved to win based on expected goals. That trend has continued this season with positive xG margins of 2.2 and 1.2 in their home games against Crystal Palace (0-0) and Manchester United (1-1) respectively.Had Smilla Holmberg not scored with her only shot of the campaign in the 95th minute against United, the situation would be even worse. While players inevitably have a small sample of shots at this point, Arsenal’s finishing woes are a collective problem. Only Lisa Baum and Alessia Russo have also scored, with the latter 1.28 goals below her expected goal tally. Scoring three goals in the international break may help Russo’s confidence.A physical deficiency may also be contributing to Arsenal’s struggles.Gradient Sportsaward players an athleticism score, a single metric which incorporates stamina, explosiveness and game context. There are 125 WSL players with a score who have played at least 270minutes this season. Steph Catley is Arsenal’s highest-ranked player, at 31st, and their only representative above 59th. Every other club has at least two players in the top 50, with Chelsea having five. West Ham possessing seven shows this is not a decisive factor in success but Arsenal fans may wonder whether their side need to increase the physical intensity.Brighton are ones to watchBrighton were predicted by Opta to finish seventh. As they are ninth, that forecast looks reasonable enough. Yet the underlying data suggests they deserve to be third, 0.1 expected points behind City. The Seagulls endured a case of wastefulness more extreme than anything Arsenal have offered up when they drew 1-1 with Villa. Despite an expected goal count of 3.17 to 0.03 in Brighton’s favour, Lynn Wilms’s 89th-minute goal robbed them of a victory.Chart showing points and expected points for the 2026-27 Women’s Super LeagueBrighton also drew at Birmingham when leading the expected goals by 1.5 and missed four Opta-defined big chances in their 2-0 defeat atLondon City Lionesses. If they can make their dominance count, Brighton look capable of at least matching the fifth-place finish they secured in 2024-25.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionTwo promoted teams have an unexpected weaponProductive pressing tends to belong to better teams. Opta’s high turnover metric records when a team win the ball to begin a new sequence of open-play possession within 40m of the opposition goal. If you sort the 2025-26 WSL by the number of high turnovers that led to shots, the five clubs with the fewest were those that finished in the bottom five. The standings were slightly more jumbled if you looked at the percentage of high turnovers that generated shots, to assess effectiveness and efficiency, but the top four teams for this finished in the WSL top five. Promoted London City had the fourth-least productive press by this measure.Two of their successors are upending these correlations. Palace are third for shot-ending high turnovers, with 12, behind Chelsea (17) and Tottenham (15). The percentage of their possession regains in the final 40m that led to shots is the highest in the division (33.3%), with their fellow promoted side Birmingham (28.6%) next in line.Chart showing percentage of high turnovers leading to shots in the 2026-27 Women’s Super LeagueThe West Midlands club are tied with Tottenham for most goals from high turnovers, on three (while Palace have two). Birmingham’s goals were all scored by Océane Hurtré, helping propel her to joint-first in the golden boot race, with five goals.The 22-year-old French attacker won the ball for two of the three high-turnover goals, including one at Manchester City. Hurtré’s others came in the first and eighth minutes of matches against Palace and Brighton respectively, illustrating the benefit that pressing opponents early can bring.Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueWomen's footballArsenal WomenFootball tacticsLondon City LionessesBrighton & Hove Albion WomenChelsea WomenfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Infantino told by top Fifa figures to scrap or depoliticise peace prize after Trump furore | Fifa | The Guardian
description: Donald Trump is likely to end up as the only political leader awarded the Fifa peace prize after Gianni Infantino was told to make major changes or scrap it
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: Donald Trump is likely to end up as the only political leader awarded the Fifa peace prize after Gianni Infantino was told to make major changes or scrap it
Content: Gianni Infantino (right) awards the first Fifa peace prize to Donald Trump last December.Photograph: Chris Carlson/APView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino (right) awards the first Fifa peace prize to Donald Trump last December.Photograph: Chris Carlson/APFifaInfantino told by top Fifa figures to scrap or depoliticise peace prize after Trump furoreBacklash greeted award of prize to US presidentFifa committee to make recommendations this yearExclusive byMatt HughesandNick AmesFri 16 Oct 2026 04.58 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 09.53 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDonald Trump is likely to end up as the only political leaderawarded the Fifa peace prizeafter Gianni Infantino was told at Thursday’smeeting of the Fifa councilto make major changes or scrap the controversial award.The Guardian has learned that several council members demanded the award be abolished and others called for the prize to be depoliticised, with Fifa’s football social responsibility committee to make a recommendation before the next council meeting in Doha on 16 December.Apologetic Infantino ‘not fit’ to lead Fifa, claim European FA heads after meetingRead moreInfantino announced the peace prize had been handed to the social responsibility committee at the start of Thursday’s meeting. Council members returned to the subject later in a series of questions about possible conflict of interests at Fifa.There is a strong view among council members that the peace prize in its current form is tainted by association with Trump, with some raising concerns that the US president could object and create a diplomatic storm if he does not like the identity of its next recipient.Fifa’s 22-person social responsibility committee is dominated by representatives from countries loyal to Infantino so abolition may be avoided on the grounds it would represent a humiliation for the Fifa president, although there is a widespread acceptance that change is required.One council member told the Guardian the most likely outcome discussed is the reinvention of the peace prize as an award for an individual within football who has delivered exceptional work promoting social harmony and responsibility, with a provision stating it cannot be given to a politician.Article two of Fifa’s statutes prohibits any political or governmental interference in football, one of several reasons why honouring Trump last year triggered such a backlash from many members.Fifa announced the creation of its peace prize last November with a stipulation that it would “reward individuals who have taken exceptional and extraordinary actions for peace and by doing so have united people across the world”.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionTrump was given the award at the men’s World Cup draw in Washington last December, with Infantino presenting the US president with a golden trophy, a medal and a certificate, but the process behind his selection has never been made public.The social responsibility committee is expected as part of its review to set strict parameters for any surviving award, and to provide details of a nomination and selection procedure.Explore more on these topicsFifaGianni InfantinoFootball politicsDonald TrumpnewsShareReuse this content

title: Elon Musk reveals ‘world’s first flying car’ at Tesla event | Tesla | The Guardian
description: The Tesla Roadster 2 drove up a curved ramp before using SpaceX rocket thrusters to fly, flip and land
Author: Mark Sweney
Headline: The Tesla Roadster 2 drove up a curved ramp before using SpaceX rocket thrusters to fly, flip and land
Content: Tesla's redesigned 'flying car' Roadster performs a ramp-assisted mid-air flipTeslaElon Musk reveals ‘world’s first flying car’ at Tesla eventThe Tesla Roadster 2 drove up a curved ramp before using SpaceX rocket thrusters to fly, flip and landMark SweneyFri 16 Oct 2026 07.53 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 12.57 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleElon Musk has revealed Tesla’s latest model, which he claims will be the world’s first flying car, using technology from his aerospace company SpaceX to “basically fly like a rocket”.The billionaire, who hosted a demonstration of the Tesla Roadster 2 at theSpaceXrocket development and testing facility in Texas, said the sports car could go from 0 to 60mph in a record time of less than a second and had thrusters.Avideo of the eventshows the Roadster, which he said was controlled remotely “to make sure we don’t kill anyone”, driving up a curved ramp using suction to grip upside down, before using thrusters toflip, fly and land.Later in the demonstration the Roadster is seen using the jets toleap over a line of Tesla’s existing modelsand then accelerate to 60mph in record time.“Turns out the future does have flying cars,” Musk said in a post on his social media site, X, accompanying a video from the event.Speaking at the event on Thursday, Musk said: “Flying cars are real. It’s got altitude controls, thrusters and main thrusters in the rear. So it can basically fly like a rocket, it can do rolls, crazy gymnastics.”“I’m not sure it’s necessarily legal in all jurisdictions,” Musk said, adding that the prototype was “not necessarily a safety optimised car but it takes the fun meter to 11”.In 2014 Musk expressed hisscepticism about a future with flying vehicles.However, three years later he announced the development of the Roadster 2, which will go into production in 2028 and is priced in excess of $200,000, (£150,000), to create an electric sports car “to give a hardcore smackdown to gasoline cars”.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toBusiness TodayGet set for the working day – we'll point you to all the business news and analysis you need every morningEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAfter the event, aTeslareservation website for expressing interest in the two-seater Roadster 2 showed that a “performance” version of the vehicle would require a £50,000 deposit. A “thrust” version would require a $250,000 deposit.Meanwhile, a one-seater “rocket” variant with “full flight system” was labelled as being available only by invitation. The car company added that flying it was not permitted on public roads.Explore more on these topicsTeslaAutomotive industryElon MuskSpaceXTechnology sectorAeronauticsMotoringnewsShareReuse this content

title: No 10 leaves option open to impose Chinese EV tariffs if UK joins EU scheme | Trade policy | The Guardian
description: Beijing warns against ‘discriminatory’ step after France drops opposition to British role in Made in Europe package
Author: Rowena Mason
Headline: Beijing warns against ‘discriminatory’ step after France drops opposition to British role in Made in Europe package
Content: An electric vehicle production line in Ningbo, China.Photograph: Nick Carey/ReutersView image in fullscreenAn electric vehicle production line in Ningbo, China.Photograph: Nick Carey/ReutersTrade policyNo 10 leaves option open to impose Chinese EV tariffs if UK joins EU schemeBeijing warns against ‘discriminatory’ step after France drops opposition to British role in Made in Europe packageRowena Mason,Lisa O’CarrollandJasper JollyFri 16 Oct 2026 14.09 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 15.05 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNo 10 has left the door open to imposing tariffs on Chinese-made electric vehicles as part of the Made inEuropepackage, prompting a warning from Beijing that such a move would be “discriminatory”.Downing Street said on Friday that it would “welcome the objective to have the UK included in the Industrial Accelerator Act” after Francedropped its opposition to Britain joining the scheme.The aim of the rules is to curb subsidised Chinese imports by giving EU-made products preferential treatment, but the UK and others such as Norway are worried about being left at a disadvantage if excluded from the scheme.The price for joining would be aligning with the EU’s tariffs on Chinese EVs imposed by the bloc in 2024, according to a Franco-German proposal on Thursday night that said the UK would have to dynamically align with EU trade defence measures.The Chinese embassy in London said it was “firmly opposed to any discriminatory practice involving tariff hikes or restrictive measures on Chinese products”.“We have expressed serious concern to the UK side regarding the reports in question,” it said, adding that “trade protectionism runs counter to WTO rules and market principles”.This week, the business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, said he would not be coerced into aligning with the EU’s policy.However, the government has been desperate to be included in the Made in Europe package, fearing billions of pounds of trade in the car industry could be lost if the UK is locked out of supply chains in the EU.Asked whether the UK accepted it would have to put tariffs on Chinese-made vehicles in order to join Made in Europe, a No 10 spokesperson said it was “premature to speculate” on the terms of any deal with the bloc and there was “still a European process to run”.They added: “But more broadly, on the principle, the UK obviously has its own trade policy and it keeps all tariffs under review. And we work closely with the British automotive sector to make sure that that approach reflects their best interests.”Chinese EVs are increasingly popular, with BYD sales up 78% year on year in September, Chery up 660% and the lesser-known Changan up by more than 3,000% in terms of market share.EU lawmakers are expected to finalise the Industrial Accelerator Act, known as Made in Europe legislation, by the end of the year or early 2027.But MEPs have already tabled 5,100 amendments, including one embracing the UK and giving Andy Burnham time to secure the deal he wants.Earlier this week the boss of Mercedes-Benz, Ola Källenius, who is also the president of the European car trade body ACEA, warned thatlocking the UK out of legislation would amount to a “deliberate choice” by EU leadersto “hurt” the car industry across the bloc.According to the new Franco-German proposal, there would be “an opt-in to further include European partners who were part of the EU single market as of 1 January 2020”, which includes the UK and Norway.This would be provided those third countries accepted “dynamic alignment on the EU’s conditions related to third countries’ investments and on relevant EU trade defence measures”.Tariffs could help UK-based manufacturers by preventing cut-price Chinese models flooding the market but they could also push up prices for consumers and harm British manufacturers trying to sell vehicles to China in the case of an escalating trade war. About 80% of UK-made cars are exported, with more than half going to the EU and 6% to China.Earlier on Thursday the trade minister, Anas Sarwar, hinted that the UK was minded to align on tariffs. He told Politico the UK and the EU must “work together and act in lockstep” to tackle China’s dominance in the automotive sector.A car industry source said the EU “has recently shown that it is possible to have a dialogue with the Chinese and get some form of safeguarding in place” without retaliation.China opposes the expansion of EV tariffs. In the past few months it has made what European Commission officials called “bloodcurdling threats” to launch a trade war over the latest plan toimpose quotason Chinese hybrid cars.While quotas can be introduced within months under World Trade Organization rules, it could take more than a year to impose tariffs on Chinese cars, with strict processes to be followed, starting with notification of an investigation and followed by evidence-gathering and sharing over alleged harms China might be causing to the British car industry.Liam Byrne, theLabourchair of the parliamentary business committee, has said imposing tariffs on Chinese EVs would be “a small price to pay” to save the industry in both the UK and the EU.At a conference in London on Thursday night, he said the UK “urgently needs” a new strategy on China to ensure that British and European manufacturing “does not die”.Byrne, who has been leading an investigation into the UK’s position on China, was highly critical of the government’s approach, which he believes is naive and based on false hopes that China will change its export policy.“Our China strategy is simply not where it needs to be. The UK urgently needs a coherent China strategy, which it does not have today,” he said.Explore more on these topicsTrade policyElectric, hybrid and low-emission carsInternational tradeLabourChinaChinese economyTariffsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs moved to new prison after reports of a luxury lifestyle behind bars | Sean ‘Diddy‘ Combs | The Guardian
description: Disgraced music mogul moved to Pennsylvania prison after reports of perks and fight injuries at New Jersey lockup
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Disgraced music mogul moved to Pennsylvania prison after reports of perks and fight injuries at New Jersey lockup
Content: Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs at the Billboard Music Awards in Las Vegas on 15 May 2022.Photograph: Jordan Strauss/APView image in fullscreenSean ‘Diddy’ Combs at the Billboard Music Awards in Las Vegas on 15 May 2022.Photograph: Jordan Strauss/APSean ‘Diddy‘ CombsSean ‘Diddy’ Combs moved to new prison after reports of a luxury lifestyle behind barsDisgraced music mogul moved to Pennsylvania prison after reports of perks and fight injuries at New Jersey lockupAssociated Press and Agence France-PresseFri 16 Oct 2026 17.05 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 17.11 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSean “Diddy” Combs, who was convicted of prostitution-related crimes, has been moved to a federal prison inPennsylvaniaafter reports that the disgraced music producer was living the high life and was injured in a fight at hisNew Jerseylockup, according to reports.The US Bureau of Prisons (BOP) is transferring Combs, 56, from FCI Fort Dix to FCI Allenwood Low, a low-security facility south of Williamsport and about 155 miles (250km) west of New York City, a person familiar with the matter said to the Associated Press. The person was not authorized to speak publicly and did so on condition of anonymity.Agence France-Press later reported being told by a BOP spokesperson that Combs had been moved from Fort Dix to Allenwood Low.The truth about Sean Combs: ‘No is not a stopping point for him’Read moreCombs’s spokesperson, Juda Engelmayer, said “decisions about inmate placement are made by the BOP, and we are not in a position to speak to the circumstances surrounding this transfer”.“Sean remains focused on moving forward, and we hope that his time at the new facility will be productive and without unnecessary disruption,” Engelmayer said.Combs was given a four-year-and-two-month sentence for his2 July 2025 convictionon prostitution-related charges for transporting people across state lines for sexual encounters. The case featured harrowing testimony about violence and sex parties he called “freak-offs”. It was a forceful reckoning for one of music and entertainment’s most influential figures.In September, NBC Newsreportedthat Combs was continuing to enjoy aspects of his millionaire lifestyle at FCI Fort Dix, smuggling in Hennessy cognac; having fellow inmates cook, clean, make his bed and give him massages; and using a contraband cellphone to view social media and an ex-girlfriend’s nude selfies.TMZ on Wednesday thenreportedthat Combs was injured in a fight with another inmate at Fort Dix and had to be taken out of the prison for treatment. In a rare rebuttal, the BOP refuted TMZ’s report, telling the AP: “The story you are referring to is false and did not happen.”In the wake of the NBC report, Combs was placed in the prison’s special housing unit, a heavily secured part of the facility away from the general population for inmates with disciplinary issues or security concerns. He has also been docked 41 days of good-conduct credit, pushing his release date back to 2 March 2028, according to the person familiar with the matter who spoke to the AP.The second US circuit court of appeals in April heard arguments in Combs’s effort to overturn his conviction and sentence, which his lawyers argued was too harsh. The court has yet to rule.Explore more on these topicsSean ‘Diddy‘ CombsUS prisonsHip-hopUS crimeUS justice systemPennsylvaniaNew JerseynewsShareReuse this content

title: Israeli settlers attack olive farmers and Washington Post journalist in West Bank | West Bank | The Guardian
description: Settlers hurl rocks at Palestinians and beat photographer Heidi Levine as part of yearly attacks to disrupt harvest
Author: William Christou
Headline: Settlers hurl rocks at Palestinians and beat photographer Heidi Levine as part of yearly attacks to disrupt harvest
Content: Firefighters dousing a burnt car with water after Israeli settlers attacked a group of Palestinians harvesting olives near Turmus Ayya.Photograph: Ammar Awad/ReutersView image in fullscreenFirefighters dousing a burnt car with water after Israeli settlers attacked a group of Palestinians harvesting olives near Turmus Ayya.Photograph: Ammar Awad/ReutersWest BankIsraeli settlers attack olive farmers and Washington Post journalist in West BankSettlers hurl rocks at Palestinians and beat photographer Heidi Levine as part of yearly attacks to disrupt harvestWilliam ChristouFri 16 Oct 2026 12.34 EDTFirst published on Fri 16 Oct 2026 10.06 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIsraeli settlers have attacked Palestinians across the occupied West Bank in a coordinated movement to disrupt the annual olive harvest, burning cars and trees and injuring Palestinians and aWashington Postphotographer.Masked settlers wielding clubs and other weapons attacked people attempting to harvest their olives inWest Banktowns on Friday. Palestinian authorities said they recorded attacks in eight villages, and injuries among at least 20 people.1:57American photojournalist recounts Israeli settler attack in the occupied West Bank – videoIt was the latest series of attacks in a deadly campaign of Israeli settler violence against Palestinians in recent months, violence which has drawn accusations of “ethnic cleansing”, including from the British government.In the town of Abu Falah, near Ramallah,at least 80 settlers, some of whom were carrying firearms or clubs, gathered to stop Palestinians from harvesting their olives, using slingshots to hurl rocks at the farmers in view of Israeli military vehicles. When some of the Palestinians then picked up rocks to defend themselves, the Israeli military fired teargas in their direction.View image in fullscreenTeargas fired by Israeli forces.Photograph: Léo Corrêa/APThe Israeli Foreign Press Association said in a statement: “This is the latest in a long line of violent attacks by Israeli settlers against journalists and other civilians in the occupied West Bank. Yet our repeated calls for action to confront this lawlessness have been ignored by Israeli authorities.”Among those injured was the Washington Post photographer Heidi Levine, who was beaten by settlers in an attack that lasted more than 10 minutes, according to witnesses. Settlers stole her passport, phone, wallet and equipment.“I was attacked, pushed to the ground. Luckily, I had my flak jacket and helmet, otherwise I probably wouldn’t even be here, because they just kept kicking and kicking me,” Levine said from a hospital bed in Ramallah. She said the attack ended when her Palestinian colleagues intervened to save her.In a statement, the Washington Post said Levine had been wearing visible markings clearly identifying her as a journalist.The office of Israel’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, said that the facts surrounding the attack on Levine were “unclear”, suggesting the attack was the fault of “200 Arabs and far-left activists” who confronted Israeli youths. The office added that it condemned “violence against anyone”.View image in fullscreenLevine speaking to journalists in hospital after the attack.Photograph: Ali Sawafta/ReutersThere has been asurge of settler violenceagainst Palestinians over the past month. Settlers have carried out at least 170 attacks since 27 September, around the start of the annual olive harvest, according to Yesh Din, an Israeli rights group.Every year, settlers attack Palestinians trying to harvest their olives, but there has been a rise in violence this year as Israel’s elections approach at the end of October.At least four Palestinians had been killed and more than 100 others injured over the past month, Palestinian authorities said. Thousands of trees have been damaged.Israel imposed new rules on the olive harvest this year, barring Palestinians from harvesting their trees located in Area C, an area under the Israeli military’s control, which comprises most of the West Bank’s agricultural land.View image in fullscreenPalestinians and activists collecting olives after the attack on Friday.Photograph: Léo Corrêa/APThe new orders prohibit Palestinians from entering about 8,800 hectares (21,800 acres) of agricultural land – a 30% increase from the year prior – without the approval of the Israeli military.
