White also claimed responsibility for Trump’s media strategy to bypass traditional media in favor of alternative platforms within the “manosphere” catering to young men – a course of action that helped him secure reelection in November 2024.The UFC has also gone to great lengths to platform Trump and his political agenda. The organization produced a propaganda documentary on Trump calledCombatant-in-Chief, which perpetuated the lie that Trump was instrumental to the UFC’s survival during a dark period in its history. Trump welcomed the attention, basking in the admiration of the UFC’s conservative-leaning male audience. He cultivated relationships with fighters, leveraging their support to portray himself as a symbolic strongman. He has embraced the UFC’s culture of defiance, machismo and spectacle to help buttress his image as a rebel against liberal norms.Since then, the UFC has been rewarded handsomely for its loyalty, not least by becoming the first professional sports brand to host an event at the White House – a propaganda spectacle that blended patriotism with bloodlust for a night ofauthoritarian theatre.The Trump administration has also formalized its relationship with the UFC bysigning a memorandum of understandingwith the US Department of State to begin “sports diplomacy” initiatives, further integrating the promotion into official government policy and soft power strategy. The UFC also began asponsorship dealwith Anduril, a controversial defense tech start-up known for developing AI-powered war machines andsentry towersused to survey the US-Mexico border. Anduril happens to be akey beneficiaryof the Trump administration’s ongoing effort to reindustrialize the US military.The UFC continues to benefit from its allegiance to Trump, most recently through the FBI training program.The UFC-FBI program is far from unique: military and police forces around the world have undergone unarmed combat training. In 2024, the Canadian militaryorganized jiu-jitsu seminarsfor various units. Gulf states such as the UAE incorporate Brazilian jiu-jitsu practice in their military and police training. Several FBI agents also have experience with unarmed combat, including retired agent George Piro, who led the FBI’s interrogation of Saddam Hussein. After retiring from the bureau, Piro won his division at the IBJJF (International Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu Federation) World No-Gi Championship.But, even given that history, the FBI’s UFC partnership reeks of favoritism. While it remains unclear how the training program will be structured or which fighters will be selected to lead the seminars, it is worth noting that several of the UFC fighters who took part in the training seminar in March 2026 were affiliated with the Trump administration, or with Patel personally. For example, former UFC fighter Jorge Masvidal headlined a“Fighters Against Socialism”tour across Florida alongside Donald Trump Jr ahead of the 2020 election. Another trainer at the March seminar, UFC lightweight champion Justin Gaethje, stumped for Trump on numerous occasions, including at the2026 midterm convention in Dallas, where he urged Republicans to vote with the same gusto they did in 2024.Several of the fighters at the training seminar were also managed by Ali Abdelaziz, a controversial figure in the sport who once worked as aninformant for the FBI and the New York Police Department. He was recruited to work undercovercollecting intelligenceon a terrorism-linked organization named Muslims of the Americas but his covert relationship with the US government was eventually severed when agentsreportedly had suspicions about his reliability.Despite his controversial past, Abdelaziz emerged as one of the most influential managers in mixed martial arts, with a roster of clients packed with past and current UFC champions. He also established relationships with Maga operatives like Richard Grenell, who served as acting director of national intelligence under Trump in 2020, as well as with Patel. Abdelaziz used his position as a manager and public figure tocampaign for Patelto land the FBI director role, even utilizing his roster of fighters’ social media accounts to spread the word. He later attended Patel’s Senate confirmation hearing and was present at the joint UFC-FBI training seminar. Last month, Abdelaziz was picturedpartying with the FBI directorat the wedding for Trump’s former lawyer Alina Habba – despite once beingsuspected of being a double agentby the same federal agency that Patel now runs.While Patel may continue to make a case for a partnership with the UFC, the truth is that this is merely the latest example of how MMA – and the UFC in particular – have become deeply intertwined withUS politics, especially among Republicans eager to bask in the reflected glory of the literal tough guys they’re bringing into the fold.Explore more on these topicsUFCMMAFBIUS politicsTrump administrationUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Super Bowl champions slump again as Darnold’s picks cost Seahawks against Broncos | NFL | The Guardian
description: Wil Lutz kicked a 53-yard field goal in overtime as the host Denver Broncos defeated the defending ⁠Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 17-14
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Wil Lutz kicked a 53-yard field goal in overtime as the host Denver Broncos defeated the defending ⁠Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks 17-14
Content: Wil Lutz and Jeremy Crawshaw celebrate their team’s overtime win over the Seahawks.Photograph: Justin Edmonds/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenWil Lutz and Jeremy Crawshaw celebrate their team’s overtime win over the Seahawks.Photograph: Justin Edmonds/Getty ImagesNFLSuper Bowl champions slump again as Darnold’s picks cost Seahawks against BroncosSeattle Seahawks 14-17 Denver Broncos (OT)Darnold intercepted twice late in gameDenver move to 4-2 despite offensive strugglesAgenciesFri 16 Oct 2026 00.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 00.04 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleWil Lutz kicked a 53-yard field goal in overtime as the host Denver Broncos defeated the defending ⁠Super Bowl championSeattle Seahawks17-14 on Thursday night.The result means the Broncos emerged from a tough six-week season-opening stretch with a 4-2 record despite an injury-riddled roster and a shaky offense. The 3-3 Seahawks, meanwhile, lost for the second time in five days. They also matched their loss total from last season,when they won their second Super Bowl title.The winning kick was set up when Denver’s Ja’Quan McMillian intercepted a Sam Darnold pass at ⁠Seattle’s 43-yard line.Troy Aikman addresses reported rift with Joe Buck and says he is leaving ESPNRead more“A defensive battle and that’s how we wanted it, and we finished on top,” said Broncos linebacker Alex Singleton after the game.JK ⁠Dobbins and RJ ​Harvey rushed for second-quarter touchdowns for the Broncos, who won despite punting on all six of their second-half possessions, excluding a one-play ⁠kneel-down, and producing just 168 yards of total offense on the night.Denver quarterback Bo Nix completed 17 of 27 passes for 107 yards. Dobbins ⁠had a team-high 41 rushing yards on 17 attempts, and Harvey had three catches for 31 yards.Darnold went 27 of 51 for 278 yards with no ‌touchdowns and two interceptions. Jaxon Smith-Njigba made 12 receptions for 134 yards, and Emanuel Wilson rushed for 52 yards on 14 carries.The Broncos appeared to have clinched the victory when Kris Abrams-Draine intercepted a Darnold pass at the Denver 31-yard line with 1:25 remaining in the fourth quarter. However, the Broncos offense went three-and-out, taking just 28 seconds off the clock.Rashid ‌Shaheed’s 31-yard punt return set the Seahawks up at their own 46-yard line, and Darnold drove the visitors into range for Jason Myers’ tying ​34-yard field goal with three seconds left.Earlier in the fourth quarter, Seattle’s George Holani scored on a one-yard run around the right end with 5:41 remaining. A two-point conversion pass from Darnold to Shaheed in the back of the end zone pulled the Seahawks within 14-11 before they tied it as time expired in regulation.Explore more on these topicsNFLSeattle SeahawksDenver BroncosUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: College football player Tyler Ulrich dies five days after ‘traumatic injury’ during game | College football | The Guardian
description: Southern Nazarene University in Oklahoma announced the death of a player described as the ‘ultimate example of quiet strength’
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Southern Nazarene University in Oklahoma announced the death of a player described as the ‘ultimate example of quiet strength’
Content: Southern Nazarene have cancelled their game on Saturday.Photograph: Charlie Riedel/APView image in fullscreenSouthern Nazarene have cancelled their game on Saturday.Photograph: Charlie Riedel/APCollege footballCollege football player Tyler Ulrich dies five days after ‘traumatic injury’ during game21-year-old was treated on field after injury during gameCoach pays tribute to player’s ‘quiet strength’Associated PressFri 16 Oct 2026 00.12 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSouthern Nazarene University inOklahomaannounced on Thursday that sophomore safety Tyler Ulrich has died five days after sustaining what the school called a “traumatic injury” during a game against Ouachita Baptist. Ulrich was 21.The Division II school based in Bethany, Oklahoma, did not reveal the cause of death or the nature of Ulrich’s injury. Ulrich was hurt during a 49-14 loss on Saturday, with the game delayed for nearly an hour while he received medical attention before being transported to a hospital.My son’s death during a college football workout was preventable. Lessons must be learnedRead more“It is with heavy hearts that we share the loss of our SNU football player, Tyler Ulrich,” the SNU Athletics said in a post on its X account. “This loss is deeply felt across our campus. Our hearts are with his family, friends, teammates, and everyone who knew him. We ask that you join us in lifting them up in prayer.”SNU coach Dustin Hada also posted a tribute on X: “Man of God, ultimate example of quiet strength, loyal, worker, joyous. That’s who Tyler was!!”The school’s president, Keith Newman, said Ulrich died in the hospital “surrounded by the love, prayers, and presence of his family, teammates and dear friends.”On Tuesday, SNU held a campuswide prayer chapel in honor of Ulrich.Ulrich, who was from Azle, Texas, was in his third season at SNU and had 16 starts in 20 games, including six starts this year. He ranked third on the team with 36 tackles.Southern Nazarene have canceled their game at Southwestern Oklahoma State on Saturday.Explore more on these topicsCollege footballCollege sportsOklahomaUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: ‘It’s really not a drama’: Carrick sticks to the script after Martínez storm | Michael Carrick | The Guardian
description: The Manchester United head coach produced a masterclass in dialling down emotion before a tricky trip to Leeds on Sunday
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: The Manchester United head coach produced a masterclass in dialling down emotion before a tricky trip to Leeds on Sunday
Content: Michael Carrick stayed in control during his press conference on Friday despite the first crisis of his managerial reign.Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMichael Carrick stayed in control during his press conference on Friday despite the first crisis of his managerial reign.Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesMichael Carrick‘It’s really not a drama’: Carrick sticks to the script after Martínez stormManchester United head coach produced a masterclass in dialling down emotion before a tricky trip to LeedsJamie JacksonFri 16 Oct 2026 15.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 15.16 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick returned his most impressive performance precisely when required as he took questions in the midst of the first crisis engulfing him as Manchester United’s manager.His team are bombing in the league after theclub’s poorest start since 1986andout of the Carabao Cup, and after Tuesday’s Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid Lisandro Martínez showed up ruptures at United bycalling out the director of football, Jason Wilcox.All of this two months into a first full campaign piloting United after last term ended so rosily for the former United midfielder.Carrick brushes off Martínez’s failure to apologise publicly to United director WilcoxRead moreOn the final day of last season,United won 3-0 at Brightonand Carrick secured an impressive third-place finish, 48 hours afteragreeing a two-year dealto continue as head coach.By last Saturday, United had six points from the first six games after drawing 1-1 with Tottenham at Old Trafford, placing Carrick’s job in jeopardy as the walls closed in on him a fortnight before the clocks go back.A game at Leeds in January proved to be Ruben Amorim’s last in charge at Manchester United after he greeted the 1-1 draw by demanding his colleaguesin the recruitment department “do their job”. With an uncanny circularity Carrick heads to Elland Road on Sunday after Martínez made similar comments. Amorim’s team were sixth going into that game; Carrick’s start the weekend 13th.On Friday, though, came a masterclass from Carrick in dialling down emotion as Martínez’s explosive comments about Wilcox – “I expect more [investment], 100%. I expect more from our technical director” – were addressed and he repeatedly referred to the “really good feeling” at the club.“It’s really not a drama for us as a group,” he said. “The boys have trained really well. This morning there was a really good feeling around the squad … so we’ve moved on pretty quickly.”If this seems less than credible, and almost certainly a stance coached by United’s PR mandarins, what else would Carrick be expected to say? More obvious was how the zen-like performance required from the club’s leader was being delivered. Even when he broke from the script to interrupt an inquisitor this strengthened the sense of Carrick being in control – hardly easy giventhe heightened glare on Unitedsince Tuesday evening.When the positive vibes trope was challenged by a questioner saying: “We’ll have to take you at face value”, Carrick’s interjection came with a smile. “I’m telling you the truth when I say that,” he said. “Do you not believe me, no? The players totally believe me. I’m telling you the truth. The squad today was in a fantastic place, better than I’ve seen it for a while, actually, and that’s it, plain and simple, you know? We’re emotional, we’re passionate, we care a lot.”When signing on to be the permanent United manager, Carrick had overseen only 21 games at elite level – in two caretaker spells at the club. United had 17 league games to play when he replaced Amorim, and Carrick has shown signs of faltering this season when having to compete on four fronts.Elimination by Brighton at the earliest stage of the Carabao Cup was not a great calling card regarding an ability to juggle competitions, and there was a surprising reaction from him after the2-0 opening-day loss at Hull. He bridled at the suggestion United had lacked “passion” during a first-half horror show. “Oh come,” Carrick said. “That’s ridiculous.”View image in fullscreenLisandro Martínez caused controversy for his post-match comments after Manchester United’s Champions League defeat at Atlético Madrid.Photograph: Florencia Tan Jun/Uefa/Getty ImagesA faulty United rearguard is hampering an attack that is functioning far better and has the most shots (125) and most touches in the opposition box (205) in the Premier League. Nine goals from six matches is not paltry but greater ruthlessness would transform a promising front six into a potent one. Carrick has to find the right blend from Benjamin Sesko, Matheus Cunha, Bryan Mbeumo, Marcus Rashford, Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes, Kobbie Mainoo, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos and Carlos Baleba.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionBaleba has sparkled in his first two appearances – against Spurs and Atlético – and might have provided the shield from the No 6 berth to ensure a less leaky defence had he not arrived injured.This has to be the hope for Carrick. Playing Tielemans at No 10 at Atlético suggests the manager may doubt the 29-year-old’s legs, and questions have been raised about whether United are putting in enough of the hard yards. Their 671.4km distance covered in the league is the fifth-lowest (Arsenal’s 716.2km is the highest), and their 581 sprints the fourth-lowest (Brentford’s 765 the most).The trip to an always febrile Elland Road that saves a particular welcome for their cross-Pennines rivals presents a stern challenge. Leeds are ninth and have lost once.“It’s a great rivalry,” Carrick said, who was full of praise for his Leeds counterpart, Daniel Farke. “There’s big history between the clubs, the areas. That’s what makes these types of games special. You’ve got to embrace the history, what it means.“I’m sure it will be a fantastic atmosphere on Sunday. It brings an intensity and it’ll be a little bit extra again, on Sunday against us … Of course, we have to be ready, and the boys will be.”Carrick requires a positive result, though in denying this, he again sounded the right note. “I don’t need results, we all need results,” he said. “It’s not about me. Manchester United is a lot bigger than any individual, bigger than me, bigger than any player, anyone else who works at this club. It’s not about me, so please …“I don’t go into every day at work, in this situation, this game, thinking about me. It’s about what we stand for, what we live for, the history, the things that we need to live up to, and that’s what drives us. So whatever’s best for the club and for the team on Sunday is the most important thing.”Explore more on these topicsMichael CarrickManchester UnitedfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Premier League news: go bananas: Maresca loving fans’ show of defiance; Alonso backs his defence | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Manchester City manager embraces response to external criticism while Chelsea coach says ‘clean sheets will come’
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Manchester City manager embraces response to external criticism while Chelsea coach says ‘clean sheets will come’
Content: Manchester City fans celebrate at Liverpool.Photograph: Michael Regan/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenManchester City fans celebrate at Liverpool.Photograph: Michael Regan/Getty ImagesThe talkManchester CityPremier League news: go bananas: Maresca loving fans’ show of defiance; Alonso backs his defenceManchester City manager embraces response to external criticism while Chelsea coach says ‘clean sheets will come’Guardian sportFri 16 Oct 2026 17.30 EDTFirst published on Fri 16 Oct 2026 12.53 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google1.City manager says ‘we need to make our noise’Enzo Maresca has called on Manchester City fans to bring inflatable bananas to help inspire the team in their first Premier League home game since being foundguilty of financial breacheswhen they take on Ipswich on Saturday. Supporters packed the away end at Liverpool with the novelty items as a nod to the club’s history last weekend.Blow-up bananas becamepopular among City fans in the 1980s and 1990swhen they spent time in the second and third tiers, and have been revived in reaction to the threat of being punished with relegation and to show there is plenty to reflect on before the 2008 takeover.“Very nice,” Maresca said of the inflatables. “I didn’t know the history behind the banana. I hope tomorrow I can see many bananas in the stadium. I think it creates a nice environment for the fans and for everyone that is in the stadium. I have four kids, they already asked me [for bananas], but tomorrow they’re going to be at the stadium and we’ll see.”It comes after Maresca dropped points for the first time as City manager,losing 4-2 to Paris Saint-Germainin the Champions League. City are three points clear of second-placed Arsenal at the top of the Premier League and victory would make Maresca the first manager to win their first seven Premier League games with a club. City are playing against a backdrop of being the focus of anger around the country.“We need to try to make our noise,” Maresca said. “And to make our noise means win at Anfield, try to win tomorrow. And this is the way we can make our noise. The different kind of noise, we are not able to control that. I think Rúben [Dias] said that people don’t like the City win. But we like to win. So I think that is a good message for everyone. Probably since the noise, we can see, I can see from my personal point of view, the fans, the club, the team, more together for sure. But we’ll see.”Will Unwin2.Alonso insists ‘the clean sheets will come’Xabi Alonso has stressed the importance of clean sheets as he strives to find the right balance at Chelsea and faces up to the absence of Reece James for three months after knee surgery. The manager has been delighted with the attacking output of his team but it is a different story at the back where they have the joint-worst defensive record in the Premier League.Alonso made tactical tweaks for last Saturday’s 5-1 home win over Bournemouth when Moisés Caicedo returned in midfield to play alongside Jordan Henderson in James’s absence. Chelsea announced on Friday morning that James had undergone an operation; it compounds the captain’s reputation for bad luck where injuries are concerned.Alonso’s team defended deeper against Bournemouth and were compact in a 4-4-2 shape out of possession rather than their usual three centre-half system. There were positive signs, which Alonso is determined to build on at Everton on Saturday lunchtime.View image in fullscreenReece James has had surgery on a knee injury picked up in training before last weekend’s 5-1 win against Bournemouth.Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters“You need a lot of clean sheets to win trophies,” he said. “But you [also] need to score a lot of goals. So it’s about being strong in defence, being good in attack and we are in that process. We are still early days; to do a very deep analysis, it’s too early. We can maybe talk in February. Those tweaks … they need to come naturally and we are not in that moment yet.“The obsession is to win and to compete in the best possible way. The clean sheets will come, I’m pretty sure of that, because we want to play with good balance and good control.”The chemistry in midfield will be key and if Caicedo’s partnership with Henderson showed promise against Bournemouth, Alonso made it clear he would also count on Roméo Lavia and Valentín Barco. He added there would be matches where he played with three midfielders.“In terms of personalities, Moi and Hendo match very well,” Alonso said. “Hendo has this energy to go. He’s very active. He covers a lot of the pitch. And to find the balance with Moi … that he’s more in the position, that he has this stability to be in good distances with everything, it was a good start.“Roméo is in a good moment. He played very well with Belgium [during the recent international window]. He’s super available. It’s been difficult for him [with injuries] but this season he’s been available and has done really well. We need to keep him with the other midfielders because that area is fundamental for our game. And also Valentín. The minutes he has played with us, he has been very competitive. He doesn’t care who is the opponent. He goes. That warrior, fighting spirit he brings is very positive.”David Hytner3.Moyes backs Pickford to keep England shirtDavid Moyes believes Jordan Pickford will relish the challenge to his England place from James Trafford and remains the nation’s undisputed No 1 goalkeeper.Pickford and Trafford shared goalkeeping duties during the recent four-game international break as part of an arranged plan by manager Thomas Tuchel. The 24-year-old Leeds player is considered the biggest threat to emerge to Pickford’s long-held position with the national team but Moyes insists the Everton keeper has been sharper than ever this season.“When Jordan came back from the World Cup, it might be the best I have ever seen him,” the Everton manager said. “He was lean, he was sharp, his footwork was brilliant, he was fast across the goal and if you look at some of the saves he has made between now and then he has made a couple of brilliant, brilliant saves.“I spoke to him when he came back and said: ‘You know you have a bit of competition now with Trafford, how are you going to deal with it?’ I don’t see Jordan falling away at the moment. I think if it really mattered to England then Jordan would still be the one who was there because he makes saves. He did that in the Argentina game. He has that experience and he is not ageing.”Trafford has won plaudits for his footwork with Leeds and England. But Moyes reflected: “Jordan is a terrific kicker of the ball, he is a better kicker than Trafford, but passing is a different equation. When you talk about that, is goalkeeping now just about the passing? Or are you saying you still have to put your gloves on and make good saves and make good decisions. I think it would be hard to move Jordan off that role. I don’t think Jordan is moving aside at the moment.”Andy Hunter4.Iraola shares delight at coaching NgumohaAndoni Iraola has said it is “a privilege” to work with Rio Ngumoha and believes the Liverpool winger is on the path to becoming an elite talent. Ngumoha has shown his versatility this season, with the arrival of the £123m Bradley Barcola prompting Iraola to shift the 18-year-old to the right wing on occasion. Ngumoha helped create Barcola’s first goal for Liverpool when impressing from that position in the midweek Champions League rout of Lask.“For us it is a privilege to have Rio in the team because he has just become 18,” said the head coach. “He has already played some minutes with the national team and that is not normal. Normally you start playing with the national team when you are 20-something and you already have matured a little bit. We have to help him because luckily for us he is not the finished product. He can still improve because he is still 18 and I hope we can help him with these processes.”View image in fullscreenTrey Nyoni is likely to make his full Premier League debut for Liverpool at Brentford.Photograph: Adam Vaughan/EPANgumoha won his third cap for England during the recent international break, featuring in both wins over Czechia in the Nations League, and has started four times for Liverpool under Iraola. “I think he knows he is elite at certain things,” Iraola said. “If you want to put someone one versus one then Rio is one of the best players you would choose because he is so difficult to contain.“There are areas he has to improve, especially without the ball. He has to get used to the demands of the Premier League in terms of duels and this happens when you come from the youth system. There you are used to being superior to the others and now you face very strong opposition and it is not easy to sustain those duels, but he is improving a lot. Body-wise he is becoming stronger and I think he is in a good place.”Andy Hunter5.Gibbs-White a doubt for Arsenal encounterNottingham Forest are sweating on the fitness of Morgan Gibbs-White before Sunday’s clash with Arsenal. The England international picked up a “minor” calf injury in last weekend’sdefeat at Crystal Palaceand will be assessed before the visit of the champions.“Morgan Gibbs-White is a doubt, he couldn’t train the entire week with us,” the manager, Oliver Glasner, said. “But it looks like he can join tomorrow’s session. He had an individual session today with our rehab coaches. Then we have to see how he reacts today and how he deals with tomorrow’s session, and then how we take the final decision.”Forest will also assess Nikola Milenkovic, who has returned to training after a bone bruise. “Milenkovic trained for the first time today,” Glasner said. “Let’s see now how he reacts. He could be in the matchday squad, but let’s see, because he’s now out for several weeks.”Press AssociationExplore more on these topicsManchester CityThe talkChelseaLiverpoolEvertonNottingham ForestnewsShareReuse this content

title: Mikel Arteta defends job cuts at Arsenal to help club ‘evolve and create success’ | Arsenal | The Guardian
description: Up to 60 jobs are a risk at Arsenal following a cost-cutting review with the news coming soon after the manager had signed a new deal worth more than £20m a season
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Up to 60 jobs are a risk at Arsenal following a cost-cutting review with the news coming soon after the manager had signed a new deal worth more than £20m a season
Content: Mikel Arteta says he is ‘not the right person’ to talk about potential job cuts at Arsenal.Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMikel Arteta says he is ‘not the right person’ to talk about potential job cuts at Arsenal.Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesArsenalMikel Arteta defends job cuts at Arsenal to help club ‘evolve and create success’Up to 60 roles at risk after structural reviewArteta signed new deal worth more than £20m a seasonEd AaronsFri 16 Oct 2026 11.03 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 16.07 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMikel Arteta has defended Arsenal’s decision to cut up to 60 jobs and insisted it was felt to be necessary to ensure they can continue achieving success.The Premier League champions are understood to have informed the staff whose positions are at risk after a consultation process started by Boston Consulting Group (BCG) before the end of last season.Arsenalhope the number of redundancies can be reduced and will attempt to redeploy affected employees wherever possible, although some job losses may be unavoidable.Carrick includes Martínez in squad; Maresca feels ‘no stress’; Watford sacking reports ‘fake news’: football – liveRead moreIt is understood the catering and travel departments are among the affected, and that the men’s and women’s first-team performance and coaching staff will not be impacted. The academy, Arsenal Women, Arsenal in the Community, the Arsenal Foundation and site security teams are also exempt, although other areas of the wider football operation are included in the review, which was overseen internally by the managing director, Richard Garlick.The timing of the proposed cuts has attracted scrutiny after last week’s announcement of Arteta’s new contract, worth more than £20m a season. Arsenal say the restructuring process began before the deal was announced and the manager said he was not the appropriate person to answer questions about the redundancies.“It was explained to me about the exercise, and the analysis that has been done across the club, and with the intention always to evolve to improve,” he said. “Some decisions have to be taken, to put people in the right roles, and keep investing to achieve what we want to achieve and the success that we want to create. So that has been explained. Obviously I am not the right person to answer that question. That’s for sure. And hopefully everybody will respect that.”The club refused to allow Arteta to answer any more questions on the subject. Arsenal’s most recent financial accounts, for the 2024-25 campaign, show that operating costs rose from £148m the previous year to £201m, with the owner, Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, keen to cut costs despite winning the Premier League title in May.Arteta was instrumental in reshaping Arsenal’s medical department over the summer, when the former Aston Villa team doctor Arnaldo Abrantes arrived, and is believed to have bolstered his backroom staff in other areas.Arsenal travel to Nottingham Forest on Sunday – the first of four away games in their next five matches – and Kai Havertz is again expected to start ahead of Viktor Gyökeres. The Sweden striker has yet to find the net for Arsenal this season and struggled against Lille in midweek after scoring four goals on international duty.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“These are moments in a player’s career, or in a season, I would say,” Arteta said. “And we are trying to help him as much as possible. The other day, I think he had some very good moments. He’s three or four times in front of goal with no keeper and the ball should arrive to him and it doesn’t. But these are the strikers. It’s very small margins. Scoring or not scoring changes the narrative, for sure, not the perception of how much he can help the team.”Explore more on these topicsArsenalMikel ArtetanewsShareReuse this content

title: The Florian Wirtz mystery: why has he not found Leverkusen form at Liverpool? | Liverpool | The Guardian
description: Two of our writers pick over the German’s contribution to Liverpool and what the £116m forward could yet produce
Author: Andy Hunter
Headline: Two of our writers pick over the German’s contribution to Liverpool and what the £116m forward could yet produce
Content: Shadow of himself: Florian Wirtz celebrates while playing for Bayer Leverkusen in 2024 and looks dejected after Liverpool conceded a second goal at Newcastle in 2026.Composite: Guardian Pictures; EPA-EFE/Shutterstock; Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenShadow of himself: Florian Wirtz celebrates while playing for Bayer Leverkusen in 2024 and looks dejected after Liverpool conceded a second goal at Newcastle in 2026.Composite: Guardian Pictures; EPA-EFE/Shutterstock; Getty ImagesLiverpoolThe Florian Wirtz mystery: why has he not found Leverkusen form at Liverpool?Two of our writers pick over the German’s contribution to Liverpool and what the £116m forward could yet produceAndy HunterandAndy BrassellFri 16 Oct 2026 12.40 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 12.42 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleIs Wirtz struggling at Liverpool as badly as most outside observers believe?Some criticism has been OTT and a fee rising to £116m heightens demands but, yes, compared with his performances in Germany and for Germany Wirtz has underwhelmed at Liverpool. The past week has encapsulated his Liverpool career so far. In theChampions League rout of Laskhe was everywhere, exploiting gaps between and behind the Austrian club’s defence and knitting together a dominant display against limited opposition. In theprevious game against Manchester City, however, when Andoni Iraola needed big players to step up in the absence of Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai, Wirtz was ineffective, wasteful and withdrawn when his team were chasing the game at 0-1. It also did not help his cause that Rayan Cherki, a cheaper alternative whom Liverpool considered and passed on, completed City’s victory with a sublime goal.AHWhat are the main reasons for this?The physicality and intensity of the Premier League appear to be Wirtz’s biggest issues. He can be swamped, knocked aside, leaving Liverpool’s central midfield exposed. Iraola this week rejected the notion that the playmaker is struggling with English football, although his answer almost veered in support of the argument. “It’s not about whether they are foreign teams or English teams,” the head coach said. “It’s about different kinds of games. Some games are more comfortable, with more time to think, sometimes less. It’s not about the competition.” But, as Brentford are likely to demonstrate on Saturday, there is less time to think and little opportunity to get comfortable in the Premier League. Wirtz produced three assists in 11 Champions League games last season, the same amount as he did in 33 Premier League matches. His passing accuracy this season – from an admittedly small sample – is 80% in the Premier League and 91.5% in the Champions League.AHChart showing players with highest number of unsuccessful touches in the 2026-27 Premier LeagueDoes he have the ‘on-pitch personality’ to succeed at Liverpool?That is a question that can be levelled at many of Liverpool’s signings since the 2025 title win. The shift towards acquiring expensive “finished products” has left many pining for the hunger and spirit of emerging talent that characterised the club’s re-emergence under Jürgen Klopp. Wirtz does not have an ego to match his price tag. He is a conscientious, dedicated professional who Iraola, like Arne Slot before him, has found to be a good listener willing to put team instructions first. He is also, it seems easy to forget, only 23. Wirtz may not be a demonstrative force but he shows personality on the ball, always looking to receive it and take responsibility. His talent is clear but has not been seen consistently enough in a Liverpool shirt.AHWhat needs to happen tactically, and in general, for him to thrive at the club?Wirtz was sold on Slot’s vision for him as the central, creative force of a new-look Liverpool attack that would turn the slender wins of the title-winning season into dominant, emphatic victories. It never happened, and Slot was sacked without finding a position that best suited Wirtz. Iraola immediately confirmed Wirtz would be his No 10 and got to work on him building a close rapport with Isak. There were some promising signs before Isak got injured again. Wirtz can justifiably argue that forces beyond his control have conspired against him at Liverpool and that, as his relationship with Bradley Barcola and Isak improves, so will his end product. He would also be helped by the addition of an out-and-out defensive midfielder who could offer Wirtz licence to roam and greater protection to the Liverpool defence. Monaco’s Lamine Camara, whose proposed move to Chelsea collapsed on deadline day, is of interest.AHHow good was Wirtz at Bayer Leverkusen?Unbelievably so. In his final two seasons in theBundesligayou could make the case that he was the best player in it. He racked up goals and assists in European competition too (he was excellent in the Champions League in 2024-25 before injury halted him in the knockouts) but you can’t just describe it in terms of numbers. He dominated the big matches and acted as the conductor of Leverkusen’s orchestra. Teams who tried to kick him out of games almost universally failed, making the idea he can’t hack the Premier League physically a flawed explanation for his difficulties.ABChart showing leading players for combined goals and assists in the Bundesliga across 2023-24 and 2024-25How much of his success was down to ‘on-pitch personality’?Partly it was, but on a technical and tactical level his success was also partly down to the freedom Xabi Alonso allowed him. As Alonso said in November 2023 (during Leverkusen’sunbeaten double-winning season) every player had responsibility to patrol an allotted zone “but Flo is different” – he was given licence to prod opposing defences as he saw fit. Alonso’s rotation of him made sure he remained fresh and impactful, his hat-trick in the 5-0 win over Werder Bremen that clinched the title in 2024 coming after he was brought on as a half-time substitute.ABskip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIs the Bundesliga being weaker than the Premier League a factor?I don’t think we can say that isn’t a factor – but this is something Wirtz himself predicted. Many in his entourage thought he would be better served by joining Bayern Munich instead of Liverpool and he acknowledged he was taking the tougher option. He knew it was a risk but was determined to challenge himself. Another point is how different the Bundesliga is tactically; it has a similarly high tempo but is far more chaotic, which is perfect for a player with hissang froidto exploit.ABChart showing median Opta team strength rating of the clubs in Europe’s big five leaguesHe shone recently for Germany. Is he being used in a notably different way?He has been given greater freedom (and a little less responsibility off the ball), more akin to his Leverkusen role, but what has been important is having Klopp cheerlead for him. The manager has not missed an opportunity to say how great Wirtz is or how his good international form is “good for Liverpool”. Klopp also gave him the captaincy for the last game (and a half), showing Wirtz and the world that he believes not only in his talent and influence but in him as a leader. It feels like the more contact he has with Klopp, the better for him and his club.ABDo you have faith in Wirtz being a success at Liverpool?Wirtz can be a class act, a lovely footballer to watch, and it would be premature to write off a gifted talent who – as the previous answer about Isak and a defensive midfielder suggests – has not had the platform to fully express himself at Liverpool. But the question of whether the Premier League suits him and whether he suits this Liverpool team continues to gnaw away. Wirtz needed a strong start to the season after the difficulties of his debut campaign at Anfield and, with one assist and no goals in six Premier League appearances, that has not materialised. There was encouragement in his overall performance and in his understanding with Barcola against Lask, as there has been on several Champions League nights, but Iraola needs his playmaker to produce a repeat in games such as Brentford away. Wirtz will remain categorised as a luxury player if another difficult Premier League assignment passes him by.AHMaybe. The deck has been largely stacked against him since he arrived: there were too many changes to a champion team in the summer he arrived, plus he was expected to pull the strings in a side that still had Mohamed Salah. He has overcome big setbacks before, such as the 2022 anterior cruciate ligament injury that took a long while to get over, so he has the character to go with his class. Wirtz has the ability to succeed at Anfield but unless the conditions around him change I think it will be very hard to do so (I can imagine him being great for Bayern in a couple of years, post-Michael Olise).ABExplore more on these topicsLiverpoolBayer LeverkusenBundesligaEuropean club footballfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Wolves’ Chirewa extends Burnley’s home woes as Vardy’s strike is in vain | Championship | The Guardian
description: Burnley took the lead via Jamie Vardy’s fist goal for the club but Wolves fought back to win 2-1 and make it 21 games at Turf Moor without a win for the hosts
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Burnley took the lead via Jamie Vardy’s fist goal for the club but Wolves fought back to win 2-1 and make it 21 games at Turf Moor without a win for the hosts
Content: Tawanda Chirewa reacts after putting Wolves ahead in the second half.Photograph: Brett Patzke/WWFC/Wolves/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenTawanda Chirewa reacts after putting Wolves ahead in the second half.Photograph: Brett Patzke/WWFC/Wolves/Getty ImagesChampionshipWolves’ Chirewa extends Burnley’s home woes as Vardy’s strike is in vainPress AssociationFri 16 Oct 2026 17.45 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 18.44 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Wolves substitute Tawanda Chirewa struck within seconds of coming off the bench as César Peixoto’s side came from behind to extend Burnley’s home misery at Turf Moor to 21 games without a win.Chirewa had just replaced Sean Neave in the 72nd minute when Mateus Mané pounced on Igor Julio’s heavy touch and sent the 23-year-old Zimbabwe international through to strike an angled shot, which flew into the net despite Grégoire Coudert getting his hands to the effort.It was a vital victory for the visitors, who had fallen behind to Jamie Vardy’s first Burnley goal before levelling through Fer López.Football Daily | Watford, a ‘fake news’ sacking and an apology to Elton JohnRead moreFor Burnley it was a huge blow. Their last league win at home was when they beat Leeds in the Premier League on 18 October, meaning their horror run will extend beyond a year. Sheffield Wednesday established an unwanted English Football League record last season by going 23 games without a win at Hillsborough.Burnley’s head coach, Nicky Hayen, admitted he does not know what the future holds for him. “I will not give up,” he said. “I am not thinking about [the future] because I don’t want to lose energy. That’s a question for other people.“We played with a lot of courage in the first half, scored one good goal, and could have scored more. But then we made a mistake before half-time and it gave the opponent energy.“It was more equal in the second half, but Wolves didn’t create many chances until we made another mistake. Then you could feel the atmosphere change in the stands – and I understand why.”Burnley’s next home game is against Portsmouth, with bitter rivals Blackburn then scheduled to visit Turf Moor on 22 November. The Clarets were denied victory on home soil on Tuesday night when Ivan Mesik equalised for Charlton in the sixth minute of added time.Vardy, who celebrates his 40th birthday in January, illustrated that his finishing instincts are as sharp as ever with a low 20th-minute strike that gave Wolves keeper José Sá no chance.View image in fullscreenJamie Vardy gives Burnley an early lead.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAHowever, the home side failed to turn their first-half superiority into more goals and were hit by a sucker punch when a mistake by the captain, Kyle Walker, led to López side-footing an equaliser before the break.Wolves, weakened by an injury crisis that worsened this week when Raúl Jiménez and Adam Armstrong joined the list of absentees, travelled north having lost their previous two games. They improved after half-time and Coudert saved Fer’s free-kick and Rafiki Saïd’s snap shot, before Chirewa came on to score the winner.“Sometimes substitutions don’t work and sometimes they do,” said Peixoto. “The important thing is that the players are ready for when they come on. They must have the right mentality to help the team – and Tawanda showed he has the right mentality. It is an important three points, but that’s all it is.”Tommy Doyle spurned a golden chance to add gloss to the scoreline late on, but Wolves held on for three much-needed points before boos rang around Turf Moor at the final whistle.Explore more on these topicsChampionshipBurnleyWolverhampton Wanderersmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Infantino told by top Fifa figures to scrap or depoliticise peace prize after Trump furore | Fifa | The Guardian
description: Donald Trump is likely to end up as the only political leader awarded the Fifa peace prize after Gianni Infantino was told to make major changes or scrap it
Author: Matt Hughes
Headline: Donald Trump is likely to end up as the only political leader awarded the Fifa peace prize after Gianni Infantino was told to make major changes or scrap it
Content: Gianni Infantino (right) awards the first Fifa peace prize to Donald Trump last December.Photograph: Chris Carlson/APView image in fullscreenGianni Infantino (right) awards the first Fifa peace prize to Donald Trump last December.Photograph: Chris Carlson/APFifaInfantino told by top Fifa figures to scrap or depoliticise peace prize after Trump furoreBacklash greeted award of prize to US presidentFifa committee to make recommendations this yearExclusive byMatt HughesandNick AmesFri 16 Oct 2026 04.58 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 09.53 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDonald Trump is likely to end up as the only political leaderawarded the Fifa peace prizeafter Gianni Infantino was told at Thursday’smeeting of the Fifa councilto make major changes or scrap the controversial award.The Guardian has learned that several council members demanded the award be abolished and others called for the prize to be depoliticised, with Fifa’s football social responsibility committee to make a recommendation before the next council meeting in Doha on 16 December.Apologetic Infantino ‘not fit’ to lead Fifa, claim European FA heads after meetingRead moreInfantino announced the peace prize had been handed to the social responsibility committee at the start of Thursday’s meeting. Council members returned to the subject later in a series of questions about possible conflict of interests at Fifa.There is a strong view among council members that the peace prize in its current form is tainted by association with Trump, with some raising concerns that the US president could object and create a diplomatic storm if he does not like the identity of its next recipient.Fifa’s 22-person social responsibility committee is dominated by representatives from countries loyal to Infantino so abolition may be avoided on the grounds it would represent a humiliation for the Fifa president, although there is a widespread acceptance that change is required.One council member told the Guardian the most likely outcome discussed is the reinvention of the peace prize as an award for an individual within football who has delivered exceptional work promoting social harmony and responsibility, with a provision stating it cannot be given to a politician.Article two of Fifa’s statutes prohibits any political or governmental interference in football, one of several reasons why honouring Trump last year triggered such a backlash from many members.Fifa announced the creation of its peace prize last November with a stipulation that it would “reward individuals who have taken exceptional and extraordinary actions for peace and by doing so have united people across the world”.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionTrump was given the award at the men’s World Cup draw in Washington last December, with Infantino presenting the US president with a golden trophy, a medal and a certificate, but the process behind his selection has never been made public.The social responsibility committee is expected as part of its review to set strict parameters for any surviving award, and to provide details of a nomination and selection procedure.Explore more on these topicsFifaGianni InfantinoFootball politicsDonald TrumpnewsShareReuse this content

title: Álvaro Arbeloa’s push to make Fulham free-flowing is floundering already | Fulham | The Guardian
description: Spanish head coach will be under huge pressure if he comes unstuck again at home to Hull on Saturday
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: Spanish head coach will be under huge pressure if he comes unstuck again at home to Hull on Saturday
Content: Álvaro Arbeloa’s Fulham team lost at Ipswich last weekend and next face the other two promoted clubs, Hull and Coventry.Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenÁlvaro Arbeloa’s Fulham team lost at Ipswich last weekend and next face the other two promoted clubs, Hull and Coventry.Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesFulhamÁlvaro Arbeloa’s push to make Fulham free-flowing is floundering alreadySpanish head coach will be under huge pressure if he comes unstuck again at home to Hull on SaturdayJacob SteinbergFri 16 Oct 2026 06.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 11.14 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleFulham fans fretting about life under Álvaro Arbeloa will not feel any better when they remember how things were under Marco Silva, who was one of the most effective managers in the Premier League when it came to making substitutions.Silva’s substitutes were involved in the fourth-highest goal contributions last season and the most in the 2024-25 season. Fulham knew how to dig in and salvage unlikely points. But Silva left last summer, joining Benfica after concluding he could achieve nothing more at Craven Cottage, and his replacement is already under pressure after some puzzling tactical choices.Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekendRead moreThe worrying shift under Arbeloa was evident during Fulham’scollapse against Ipswichlast weekend. The west Londoners were 1-0 up and looking good for their first league win of the season when Arbeloa weakened his midfield by replacing Shea Charles with Manuel Ángel in the 70th minute.It was a strange way to shut up shop. Charles is physically imposing, has impressed since joining from Southampton and was doing well alongside Sander Berge. The 22-year-old Ángel is 5ft 7in, was making his Premier League debut and has little experience of senior football. Ipswich’scomeback to win 2-1was not a surprise, particularly when Arbeloa’s other rejigs included bringing on Rodrigo Muniz and switching from a 4-2-3-1 system to a flat 4-4-2 in an attempt to defend the lead.The subsequent floundering felt inevitable. Emile Smith Rowe, another late substitute, was slow to close down Abdoul Ouattara when the Ipswich right-back equalised. Fulham have dropped eight points from winning positions. They are managing games badly and their physical shortcomings were exposed by Ipswich, whose winner came from a poorly defended free-kick and left Fulham in last place before facing Hull at home on Saturday.Chart showing current favourites for relegation from the Premier LeagueArbeloa needs a win. Relegation fears are growing and there are whispers that the Spaniard’s job is under threat. Fulham had a tricky start – they have already faced Chelsea, Liverpool and Manchester United – but the Ipswich game was supposed to mark a turning point. It was the first of three consecutive meetings with the promoted sides and, with Coventry, Hull and Ipswich surpassing expectations, it is easy to see Fulham’s aim to move to a more expansive style under Arbeloa backfiring.Questions have to be asked over the decision by the Khan family to appoint someone whose experience of management was limited to an interim spell in charge of Real Madrid last season. Fingers will be pointed at the succession planners. Tony Khan, director of football and son of patriarch Shahid, has faced fierce criticism in the past. Silva offered stability. There was always a fear the project would fall apart once the Portuguese was gone.View image in fullscreenGonzalo García struggled to make an impression at Ipswich.Photograph: Chris Radburn/ReutersIt does not help Arbeloa to lean on his time at the Bernabéu. He responded to a question about pressure after losing to Ipswich by saying: “I played for the best team in the world … I have coached the best team in the world.” But the optics are awkward. Arbeloa did not win anything as Madrid’s manager, his comments risk making it seem his current employers should be grateful to have him and eyebrows have been raised at three of the 43-year-old’s summer signings coming from his former club.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionÁngel, César Palacios and Gonzalo García were all promising young Real Madrid players, all share representation with Arbeloa and are now adapting to a new league. Palacios, an inventive passing midfielder, is 21 and Garcia, a nimble forward, is 22. They deserve to be given time, although the clock is ticking. García, signed for £40m, has one league goal from 18 shots and struggled against Ipswich, winning few duels and pressing ineffectively.Supporters are growing restless. They wonder why Kevin, the Brazilian winger, is being used on the right rather than the left. They feel Arbeloa is chopping and changing too often. They worry about the team conceding costly late goals against Sunderland, Crystal Palace and United. Fulham were ridiculously open in their opening game,the barmy 3-2 defeat by Chelsea, and their expected goals against is 10.3 in six games. They have lost two of their main goalscorers, Raúl Jiménez and Harry Wilson, and are struggling to fill the void.Equally there is an argument that Arbeloa needs time to implement a new style. There are suggestions some players are unsure about the manager’s tactics. Some stalwarts have been sidelined – Joachim Andersen, the influential Denmark centre-back, is not suited to playing a high line and has lost his spot to David Affengruber – but perhaps a refresh was required. Fulham have looked to lower the age of their squad, in part because of a need to comply with financial regulations, and there is nothing intrinsically wrong with trying to play more exciting football.There have been encouraging spells. After flirting with European qualification in each of the past four seasons, only to fizzle out and finish in the bottom half, Fulham can be forgiven for wondering how to take the next step. At the same time the fear for supporters is that a club operating with one of the league’s smaller budgets have forgotten what it takes to survive. Silva’s teams could attack but were gritty and streetwise. At the moment Arbeloa looks naive. Fulham lost £45m in the past financial year and spent a lot on the Riverside Stand refurbishment. The Khans need Premier League survival. Arbeloa has big ideas but might not make it past this month without a huge improvement.Explore more on these topicsFulhamHull CityfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: Watford, a ‘fake news’ sacking and an apology to Elton John | Watford | The Guardian
description: In today’s Football Daily: fun and games at Vicarage Road
Author: Michael Butler
Headline: In today’s Football Daily: fun and games at Vicarage Road
Content: Watford manager Alessio Dionisi (left) and Hornets fan and Honorary Life President Elton John.Composite: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock; Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenWatford manager Alessio Dionisi (left) and Hornets fan and Honorary Life President Elton John.Composite: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock; Getty ImagesFootball Daily newsletterWatfordWatford, a ‘fake news’ sacking and an apology to Elton JohnSign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now!Michael ButlerFri 16 Oct 2026 10.37 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 11.59 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google‘I’M STILL STANDING …’There are only two things certain in life –death and taxesReece James knack and Watford managerial news – and Football Daily’s bingo card lit up with both on Friday. But while Chelsea’s statement on their crocked right-back having successful knee surgery wasa cut-and-paste jobfrom the last time James was injured, the quotes by Watford manager Alessio Dionisi were much more exciting, mainly because it containedan actual apology to Elton Johnand the remarkable news that the club’s trigger-happy owners have not already sent the Italianthe same way as an apple in Michael Owen’s house.Having already made four managerial appointments in 2026 and 28 since the Pozzo family purchased the club in the summer of 2012, the owners have shown uncharacteristic restraint despiteWatfordwinning just three of the last 21 Championship games (even Oxford United have more victories in the division during that time despite being relegated to League One in April). Pressure on Dionisi has now increased after John – which feels like an inappropriately underwhelming way to refer to one of the most talented and flamboyant pop singers of all time – admitted he was “upset” at the club’s form in a now-deleted post on a Social Media Disgrace on Sunday.“As a lifetime supporter of Watford FC, I am very upset and disappointed at the decline over the past few weeks – I really feel for the supporters who have to watch this,” Elton crooned afterthe 4-0 home defeat to Burnley. “I’ve called the chauffeur, you little chancer”,he didn’t add. Things worsened for Dionisi on Tuesday with struggling Cardiff romping toa 5-1 winto leave the Hornets in the Championship relegation zone, with some reporting – incorrectly, as it turned out – the Italian had been sackedduringthe game. But despite the unconfirmed reports of his demise, Dionisi remains very much in post.“There is good news, bad news or fake news probably. In this case for the moment, it is fake news [that I have been sacked] but I don’t decide,” hetold the BBCon Friday, not wholly convincingly. “For Elton John, I am sorry because I don’t know him. But football is wonderful because everyone speaks [their mind]. I have been a coach for 14 years, and it is normal. In my past there was negative and there was positive moments. At the moment it is a negative moment. Inside the training ground there is only one mentality, only one street for everyone.” Absolute goosebumps, Alessio. Cheers for that. We know not of the cryptic road you speak – Vicarage?Yellow Brick?The road to nowhere? – but we’ll have to see if Dionisi becomes the latest Watford manager to find himself out on the street, kicked to the curb through a front door marked ‘Do One’, following Saturday’s visit of Charlton Athletic.QUOTE OF THE DAY“I think I have an angel on my shoulder. I’m actually fortunate to be alive at all. I was 20 and playing for Dortmund when three pipe bombs went off right next to our bus on the way to a Champions League match. A lot of young people probably would not even believe that it happened, or how bad it was, but it marked us all. There was a deafening noise, and then I remember the bus nearly tipping over. I looked behind me and saw blood on the floor. Smoke, screams. I remember being at the hospital later that night, waiting for Marc Bartra, who had his wrist badly cut up. The next day, someone told me that a huge piece of shrapnel was lodged in the headrest of the seat next to Marc. My usual seat. That day, the seat was empty. My legs were feeling a bit tight, and the seats in the front reclined. So I sat up there instead, and it may have saved my life” – Mikel Merino recalls how a last-minute change of seats on the Borussia Dortmund coach that was hit by explosives on its way to the home leg of their Champions League semi-final against Monaco in 2017 may have saved his life in a wider interview with the Player Tribune.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenPolice with the Borussia Dortmund team bus after an explosion near their hotel in 2017.Photograph: Reuters  Staff/ReutersFOOTBALL DAILY LETTERSdouble quotation markShall we just hand over the Bigger Cup to PSG now to ease the calendar congestion?” – Krishna Moorthy.double quotation markReading that ‘European football leadersare increasingly confidentthey will find a candidate to stand against Infantino next year’,I can’t be the only well informed reader to think that a certain intergalactic bin wearing member of the nobility would make a terrific candidate. Can the Big Website ‘Higher Ups’ have a word?!” – Chris Reid.double quotation markLooking at the Benfica v Celtic game I was immediately drawn to the presence of two Durans. Have there been any other instances of any other bands being present in a game? Possibly in the Human League? I am hoping a Serie A game with a Scritti and a Politti … a French game with Depeche and Mode. You get the general idea” – Mike Turney.View image in fullscreenCount Bin face: look out Gianni.Photograph: Dan Kitwood/Getty ImagesIf you have any, please send letters tothe.boss@theguardian.com.Today’s prizeless letter o’ the day goes to … Chris Reid. Terms and conditions for our competitions, when we run them, arehere.This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version,just visit this page and follow the instructions.Explore more on these topicsWatfordFootball Daily newsletterfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: British Cycling under scrutiny over allegations of ‘toxic culture’ in leadership team | Cycling | The Guardian
description: A former commercial manager criticised the handling of a bullying complaint as British Cycling insisted ‘action is taken’ when appropriate
Author: Sean Ingle
Headline: A former commercial manager criticised the handling of a bullying complaint as British Cycling insisted ‘action is taken’ when appropriate
Content: A British Cycling survey found 31% of riders and staff said they had witnessed or experienced thoughtless, inappropriate, or unacceptable behaviour.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAView image in fullscreenA British Cycling survey found 31% of riders and staff said they had witnessed or experienced thoughtless, inappropriate, or unacceptable behaviour.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PACyclingBritish Cycling under scrutiny over allegations of ‘toxic culture’ in leadership teamFormer employee alleges bullying swept under carpetBritish Cycling defends handling of complaintsSean IngleFri 16 Oct 2026 13.07 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 15.28 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBritish Cycling is facing further questions after a former employee accused it of having a “toxic culture” days afterMatt Richardson was sent homefrom the World Track Championships in Shanghai.Jack Lindsay, who worked as a commercial manager atBritish Cyclingfrom 2024 to 2025, criticised the way he claimed it responded to his formal workplace bullying complaint spanning dozens of incidents. And he also questioned what he branded a lack of oversight from UK Sport, which has given the organisation £30m to prepare for the LA Olympics.“The complaint covered dozens of incidents over six months, spanning multiple categories of alleged bullying,” Lindsay wrote in a post on LinkedIn. “Most were partially substantiated. There would be no apology, and I was told of no action against the individual I had sought to hold responsible.”Matt Richardson vows to cooperate with investigation into alleged misconductRead moreLindsay also claimed that he had “repeatedly raised incidents of bullying by a member of the executive with members of the senior leadership team, and that management had chosen to address them informally”.“It is not acceptable to continue subjecting staff to a leadership team that have perpetuated this toxic culture,” he said.Lindsay said that after he resigned the-then BritishCyclingchief executive, Jon Dutton, told him that he would commission an independent survey of the leadership culture within the GB Cycling Team.That survey, it was revealed by the Times newspaper this week, found that 31% of riders and staff were asked whether they had “witnessed or experienced thoughtless, inappropriate, or unacceptable behaviour” answered yes.Quick GuideHow do I sign up for sport breaking news alerts?ShowIn the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from theiOS App Storeon iPhone or theGoogle Play storeon Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Meanwhile when they were asked for three words to describe the culture of their world class programme, “driven” was the most commonly used word among the riders but second-most prominent, alongside “supportive”, was “toxic”.In response to a series of questions about Lindsay’s allegations, a British Cycling spokesperson said: “The wellbeing of our people is fundamental to everything we do at British Cycling. Any complaint is taken seriously and handled through our formal procedures and where appropriate, action is taken.“Out of fairness to everyone involved, we do not comment on individual cases, and the details of any action taken are kept confidential,” he added. “We recognise that raising concerns can be difficult. There are established routes available to report concerns and we continue to strengthen how we listen to and support our people.”Lindsay also drew parallels with how British Cycling’s governance and culture had been heavily criticised by Annamarie Phelps in an independent review in 2017, saying that “almost a decade later, leadership is taking the program in the same direction”.“This reflects a wider problem in elite sport, where organisational reputation and relationships with funding bodies and the individuals within can become entangled with questions of accountability,” he wrote.“The high-performance programme receives millions of pounds each year in public funding. Athletes, staff, sponsors and the public have a legitimate interest in whether the organisation upholds the standards it promotes.”However a UK Sport spokesperson said that the organisation did properly hold sports accountable and that its approach was “fundamentally and materially different to 2017”.The spokesperson added that funded sports were required to “complete a cultural assurance exercise on an annual basis,” and to develop cultural action plans to strengthen and improve their culture. UK Sport said that a team of advisers was also in place to “provide assurance on our investment”.“It is critical to us that the sports we invest in have a safe, healthy and high performing culture where athlete voice is included in decision making,” the spokesperson added. “We prioritise assuring culture within the performance programmes in which we invest as a key pillar of our approach to winning well.”Explore more on these topicsCyclingBritish CyclingnewsShareReuse this content

title: Carrick brushes off Martínez’s failure to apologise publicly to United director Wilcox | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: ‘He’s realised he’s made a mistake and that’s enough,’ said the Manchester United head coach as he defended Lisandro Martínez’s statement
Author: Jamie Jackson
Headline: ‘He’s realised he’s made a mistake and that’s enough,’ said the Manchester United head coach as he defended Lisandro Martínez’s statement
Content: ‘I understand emotion at times,’ said Michael Carrick as he backed Lisandro Martínez after the player’s outburst.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAView image in fullscreen‘I understand emotion at times,’ said Michael Carrick as he backed Lisandro Martínez after the player’s outburst.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PAManchester UnitedCarrick brushes off Martínez’s failure to apologise publicly to United director WilcoxManchester United coach accepts defender’s apology‘He’s realised he’s made a mistake and that’s enough’Jamie JacksonFri 16 Oct 2026 11.18 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 12.27 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMichael Carrick brushed off Lisandro Martínez’s failure to offer Jason Wilcox a public apology after the defender criticised Manchester United’s director of football in the wake of Tuesday’sdefeat at Atlético Madrid.Martínez referred directly to Wilcox after the 2-0 Champions League loss, saying: “I expect more from our technical director.”Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekendRead moreOn ThursdayMartínez issued an apologythat did not mention Wilcox or withdraw the essence of his outburst: the need for more squad investment. “The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise,” he said.Carrick was asked whether he respected Martínez for not saying sorry to Wilcox. “He’s released his statement, he’s realised he’s made a mistake and that’s enough for all of us to move on with,” United’s manager said.Carrick was pressed on whether it would have been better if Martínez had apologised to Wilcox and for his wider comments about investment, rather than just saying sorry for the timing and location of his interview. “From our point of view, the acknowledgment of what’s been done has certainly been enough, we’ve moved on and we’re definitely not looking back at it now,” he replied.Carrick said Martínez was available for Sunday’s trip to Leeds, where Manchester United go having taken only six points from their opening six league games. They were knocked out of theCarabao Cup by Brightonlast month and have one win and a defeat in the Champions League. Poor form has increased the pressure on Carrick, who was asked whether Martínez’s comments were an unwanted distraction that had annoyed him.“No, I understand emotion at times,” he said. “We ask for passion, we ask for emotion, we ask for fire and we ask for players to care. There’s a way of doing that, and that’s already been acknowledged, but we need to carry that intensity and that willingness and that togetherness and that spirit. As a group, we need to use it, and we’ve got to use it in the right way.”Wayne Rooney, United’s record goalscorer, claimed Martínez’s comments “will rip the dressing room apart”. It was put to Carrick that they may have an opposite, unifying effect.“There’s a lot of things that can affect the group in all sorts of different ways,” said Carrick, who went on to highlight his players’ reaction to conceding inside a minute at Atlético. “It’s one of the toughest places to play in the Champions League, so to go a goal down so early, and the way we responded shows an underlying belief and spirit and a togetherness,” he said.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionHe indicated that events on and off the pitch this week had brought the squad together. “Certain situations can galvanise the group, and it’s certainly galvanised the group as this week’s progressed. The boys are in a really good place right now.”Carrick was asked why anyone outside the club, including former players such as Rooney who have criticised Martínez, should believe there is unity. “There’s a lot of people that say a lot of things, and ex-pros or not ex-pros, it doesn’t necessarily mean you understand what’s going on here,” he said. “I’m telling you the truth. The squad today [Friday] was in a fantastic place, better than I’ve seen it for a while.”Carrick said Luke Shaw and Kobbie Mainoo faced fitness tests.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedMichael CarricknewsShareReuse this content

title: Lions lock Hyron Andrews dies at team hotel before Champions Cup game against La Rochelle | Champions Cup | The Guardian
description: Tributes have been paid to Johannesburg Lions’ Hyron Andrews after he died in the team hotel on the eve of their Champions Cup game against La Rochelle
Author: Robert Kitson
Headline: Tributes have been paid to Johannesburg Lions’ Hyron Andrews after he died in the team hotel on the eve of their Champions Cup game against La Rochelle
Content: Hyron Diego Andrews, who has died in France, played for the 10bet Lions having previously represented the KZN Sharks and Sale Sharks.Photograph: Nokwanda Zondi/BackpagePixView image in fullscreenHyron Diego Andrews, who has died in France, played for the 10bet Lions having previously represented the KZN Sharks and Sale Sharks.Photograph: Nokwanda Zondi/BackpagePixChampions CupLions lock Hyron Andrews dies at team hotel before Champions Cup game against La RochelleSA Rugby said Andrews fell at hotel in tragic accidentSquad will play on Saturday to honour teammateRobert KitsonFri 16 Oct 2026 08.35 EDTLast modified on Fri 16 Oct 2026 16.07 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTributes have been paid to Johannesburg Lions’ Hyron Andrews after he died in the team hotel on the eve of theirChampions Cupgame against La Rochelle.Andrews, 31, who also played for the KZN Sharks and Sale Sharks, could not be revived by emergency services after the alarm was raised at the Atalante-Relais Thalasso hotel on the Île de Ré. A statement from SA Rugby said the lock forward had “passed away tragically” after an accident in which he fell.“This is terrible and distressing news; our hearts go out to Hyron’s family and the whole Lions rugby community,” said Mark Alexander, president of the South African Rugby Union in a statement released after Andrews’ family had been contacted.View image in fullscreenHyron Andrews died at the Atalante-Relais Thalasso hotel the eve before the Champions Cup game against La Rochelle.Photograph: Romain Perrocheau/AFP/Getty Images“There are no words to adequately convey our shock and the depth of sympathy we feel for his wife Maighlin, and for his extended family, friends, teammates and loved ones during this time of immense sorrow.“Hyron was a respected member of the rugby community whose contribution to the game and impact on those around him will be remembered with great fondness.“His untimely passing is a devastating loss, and we share in the grief of all who knew and loved him.”The Lions had been preparing to make their debut in the top-tier tournament on Saturday having flown to Europe after a heavy 57-15 defeat by the Bulls, their South African rivals. The squad has chosen to fulfil the fixture in honour of their teammate.European Professional Club Rugby, the tournament organisers said: “In memory of Hyron, a moment’s silence will be held ahead of every Investec Champions Cup and EPCR Challenge Cup match this weekend.”Andrews, who was born in Paarl and attended Hoërskool Garsfontein in Pretoria, also represented the Junior Springboks in 2015.The Lions posted an emotional tribute on Instagram, saying: “It is with broken hearts that we mourn the passing of Hyron Andrews, a valued member of our Lions family. Our deepest condolences are with Maiglin, Hendrix, Emerson and the entire Andrews family during this incredibly difficult time.“Rest in peace, Hyron. You will always be part of our family.”Sale reflected on the loss of a “much-loved member” of their squad, who had stayed on past his initial short-term deal through to the end of the 2025-26 campaign, making 45 appearances.View image in fullscreenThe Lions will fulfil the fixture at the Stade Marcel Deflandre in honour of their late teammate.Photograph: Icon Sport/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.“Hyron was just a brilliant guy and a brilliant team-mate. He was so skilled on the field, but off it, he was always someone you would want to have a beer with,” Sharks’ director of rugby Alex Sanderson told the club’s website.“He was funny and charismatic in his own unique, dry way and the lads, to a man, loved playing with him and being around him. It was a big move for Hyron and his wife Maighlin to come to England but he truly made a second home in Manchester and it was incredible to see how he and his family embraced the club and area.”The tragic incident comes on the 10th anniversary of the death of the Munster coach Anthony Foley in a Paris hotel room in 2016. Foley, who was 42, died in his sleep on the eve of a European tie against Racing 92 after a heart condition caused fluid to build up in his lungs. Tributes are due to be paid to him before this weekend’s game against Racing in Cork, with the Munster players set to wear commemorative presentation jackets featuring the club crest and the number 8, Foley’s position.Explore more on these topicsChampions CupRugby unionLa RochellenewsShareReuse this content

title: Australia cruise past Samoa in women’s Rugby League World Cup opener | Women's Rugby League World Cup | The Guardian
description: Jillaroos defeat Fetu Samoa 40-0 in Sydney as Jocelyn Kelleher kicks six conversions on her debut
